Data were extracted from English publications on AS diagnosis from the Web of Science Core Collection (January 1, 2008-October 21, 2024). title: Androgen insensitivity syndrome: A case report.
abstract: Rationale 46, XY disorder of sex development (46, XY DSD) is relatively rare and frequently missed in clinical practice, necessitating early standardized diagnosis and treatment. Androgen insensitivity syndrome (AIS), a major subtype, should be considered in phenotypic females with suggestive clinical clues. Patient concerns A 29-year-old phenotypic female presented with primary amenorrhea and intermittent abdominal pain. Examination revealed normal breast development, sparse pubic hair, and female external genitalia. Pelvic ultrasonography and CT showed an absent uterus and ovaries, with bilateral inguinal masses. Diagnoses The case met the 3 diagnostic criteria for 46, XY DSD: 46,XY karyotype, testicular tissue, and feminized external genitalia. A diagnosis clinically consistent with complete AIS was further supported by the characteristic phenotype - female appearance, normal breast development, sparse pubic hair, and absent Müllerian structures. Other etiologies of undervirilization, including 5α-reductase deficiency and 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency, were considered. Genetic confirmation was unavailable, limiting subtype certainty. Interventions Following counseling, the patient underwent laparoscopic bilateral orchiectomy as prophylactic gonadectomy to reduce malignancy risk, together with inguinal hernia repair, followed by postoperative hormone replacement therapy. Postoperative histopathology confirmed testicular tissue with Leydig cell hyperplasia, absent spermatogenic cells, and no malignancy. Outcomes Abdominal pain resolved postoperatively, with improved psychological well-being and adaptation to the diagnosis under ongoing endocrine and psychological support. Lessons 46, XY DSD is underdiagnosed due to phenotypic variability, reliance on specialized tests, and social biases. AIS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of phenotypic females presenting with primary amenorrhea, developed secondary sexual characteristics, and an absent uterus on ultrasound. However, definitive subtyping requires AR gene sequencing, which was not available in this case. Early diagnosis requires careful assessment of newborn external genitalia, with specialist evaluation prompted by any atypical findings, and hormonal and genetic testing in adolescents with abnormal development. Multidisciplinary care - involving gynecologists, endocrinologists, surgeons, geneticists, and mental-health professionals - is essential for comprehensive management, including psychological support, hormone therapy, and timely prophylactic gonadectomy. Establishing specialized multidisciplinary centers for DSD is also recommended.

title: Pulmonary cryptococcosis mimicking metastatic progression despite systemic disease stability in advanced colon cancer: A case report and literature review.
abstract: Rationale In patients with advanced cancer, newly detected pulmonary nodules are often interpreted as metastatic progression. The distinctive feature of this case was the appearance of multiple new lung nodules during otherwise controlled systemic disease: the primary colonic lesion and hepatic metastases remained stable while tumor marker levels declined. This radiologic-clinical discordance prompted reconsideration of metastatic progression and broadened the differential diagnosis. Patient concerns A patient with advanced colon cancer, who was undergoing systemic chemotherapy and had otherwise stable disease, was found to have developed new pulmonary nodules on routine surveillance imaging. The patient was entirely asymptomatic from a respiratory standpoint. The primary clinical concern was the discordance between the radiologically suspicious findings and the patient's overall stable clinical condition. Diagnoses The initial radiologic impression favored pulmonary metastases. However, multidisciplinary review recognized the discordance between the new lung lesions and the otherwise stable systemic disease and raised concern for an opportunistic infection. Serum (1,3)-β-D-glucan and qualitative cryptococcal capsular polysaccharide antigen tests were positive, supporting a diagnosis of pulmonary cryptococcosis. Interventions After cerebrospinal fluid evaluation excluded central nervous system involvement, fluconazole 400 mg once daily was initiated. The anticancer strategy was not escalated on the basis of the pulmonary findings alone. Outcomes Follow-up chest computed tomography demonstrated marked regression of the pulmonary nodules. Lessons When new pulmonary lesions arise despite stability or response at established tumor sites, apparent radiologic progression should not automatically be equated with oncologic progression. Integrating the longitudinal treatment response, tumor marker trends, clinical symptoms, imaging features, and targeted infectious testing can prevent unnecessary changes in cancer therapy and may avoid invasive procedures when a sufficiently supported alternative diagnosis is available.

title: Biodegradable pins fixation for lateral condylar fracture of the humerus in children: A retrospective study of biodegradable pin fixation combined with versus without absorbable tension band wiring.
abstract: Biodegradable pins are increasingly used in the treatment of lateral condylar fractures of the humerus (LCFH) in children, but the strength of the biodegradable pin is weaker than that of K-wire. However, to enhance the stability of LCFH fixed by biodegradable pins, absorbable tension band wiring is often combined with the application, yet high-quality comparative evidence verifying the clinical value of this auxiliary reinforcement remains lacking. This study aimed to compare and analyze whether auxiliary absorbable tension band wiring has clinical significance for Weiss type III LCFH and to clarify whether additional tension band fixation is clinically necessary in reducing postoperative complications and improving fracture stability. This study enrolled 96 children with Weiss type III LCFH admitted between January 2017 and September 2019. The patients were divided into 2 groups: A (fixed by 3 biodegradable pins alone, n = 45) and B (fixed by 3 biodegradable pins and combined with the application of absorbable figure-of-eight tension band wiring, n = 51). Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative indicators, including age, sex, operation time, intraoperative blood loss, fracture healing time, elbow functional recovery time, and postoperative complications, were compared between the 2 groups. Postoperative elbow function was assessed by using the Flynn grading system. All radiographic measurements and functional evaluations were performed by 2 calibrated orthopedic surgeons with excellent inter-rater reliability. Sample size calculations were performed before data collection to guarantee statistical validity. There were no significant differences in age, sex, injured side, preoperative fracture displacement, operation duration, intraoperative blood loss, fracture healing time, elbow functional recovery time, or Flynn functional grading (all P > .05). Complete fracture union was observed in all patients, and no adverse complications, such as wound infection, bone nonunion, osteonecrosis, or elbow deformity, occurred in either group. Absorbable tension band wiring reinforcement is not required after biodegradable pin fixation in the treatment of LCFH in children.

title: Suspected allergic bronchopulmonary candidiasis in a patient with concurrent multidrug-resistant bacterial pneumonia: A case report.
abstract: Rationale Allergic bronchopulmonary candidiasis (ABPC) is a rare pulmonary hypersensitivity disorder; diagnosis is difficult because Candida albicans is usually a respiratory commensal. Patient concerns A 70-year-old man with hypertension and prior cerebral infarction was admitted for sudden right limb weakness (6.5 hours) and diagnosed with hemorrhagic cerebral infarction in the intensive care unit. Diagnoses Persistent fever and pulmonary infiltrates developed despite broad-spectrum antibiotics. Total immunoglobulin E (IgE) was 2181 IU/mL; sputum grew C albicans + carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa; bronchoalveolar lavage fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing detected C albicans, P aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, EBV, and HSV-1. ABPC was suspected alongside multidrug-resistant bacterial pneumonia. Interventions Ceftazidime-avibactam (2.5 g q8h) + nebulized polymyxin B (0.5 M IU q12h); oral voriconazole (400 mg q12h loading, then 200 mg q12h); IV methylprednisolone 40 mg/d. Outcomes Clinical improvement on combined therapy; respiratory stabilization within 2 weeks; intensive care unit transfer out. Follow-up chest computed tomography showed resolution of infiltrates; total IgE fell from 2181 to 995 IU/mL (-54%). Discharged with hemorrhagic cerebral infarction, hypertension, carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas pneumonia, K pneumoniae co-infection, and ABPM. Lessons Persistent infiltrates with high IgE and Candida isolation should suggest ABPM, not intensified antibiotics. ABPC can occur in older patients without asthma. Early corticosteroids plus antifungals yield rapid improvement. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing complements conventional testing but cannot confirm ABPC alone.

title: Primary pulmonary mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma presenting as a right hilar mass: A case report.
abstract: Rationale Primary pulmonary lymphoma (PPL) is an extremely rare malignant lung tumor that is frequently misdiagnosed as pneumonia or lung cancer due to its atypical radiological and clinical presentation. The rationale of this report is to elucidate the diagnostic value of combining computed tomography (CT) and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) in evaluating a rare presentation of PPL. Patient concerns A 44-year-old male was admitted after an incidental lung lesion was discovered during routine screening. He was completely asymptomatic, lacking respiratory or systemic "B symptoms." Diagnoses A baseline chest CT identified a 3.9 × 3.5 cm soft-tissue mass in the right hilar region that compressed the right upper lobe bronchus, leading to secondary post-obstructive consolidation that lacked the characteristic air bronchogram sign. The CT also revealed an incidental 2.6 × 2.6 cm anterior mediastinal nodule. Subsequent whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated intense tracer uptake in the right hilar mass with a maximum standardized uptake value of 7.1 and mild-to-moderate uptake in an adjacent regional lymph node (maximum standardized uptake value of 3.2). The scan showed completely absent uptake in the anterior mediastinal nodule and the post-obstructive consolidation, arguing against metabolically active malignancy in those areas. Histopathological and immunohistochemical analysis from a bronchoscopic transbronchial lung biopsy confirmed primary pulmonary mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma. Interventions The patient underwent localized radiotherapy targeting the right hilar mass and the FDG-avid regional hilar/posterior mediastinal lymph node. A total dose of 66 Gy was delivered in 18 fractions over the course of 3 weeks. Outcomes At the 2-month post-discharge follow-up, a repeat chest CT revealed a marked reduction in the size of both the hilar lesion and the regional lymph nodes. The patient remained completely asymptomatic, and his laboratory parameters normalized. Lessons Differentiating PPL from central lung cancer and coexisting benign mediastinal abnormalities presents a significant clinical challenge, particularly when atypical radiological features mimic aggressive carcinomas. Whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT serves as an invaluable, noninvasive modality for metabolic characterization, accurate loco-regional staging, and preventing clinical overstaging by effectively differentiating metabolically active lymphoma from concurrent benign lesions.

title: Excellent response to high-dose Riboflavin in Brown-Vialetto-Van Laere syndrome: A case report.
abstract: Rationale Brown-Vialetto-Van Laere syndrome, currently recognized within the spectrum of riboflavin transporter deficiency type 3 (RTD3), is a rare inherited neurometabolic disorder associated with pathogenic variants in SLC52A3. It typically presents with progressive sensorineural hearing loss, pontobulbar dysfunction, peripheral neuropathy, and respiratory involvement. Diagnosis may be delayed because routine metabolic and neuromuscular investigations can be unrevealing despite a characteristic clinical phenotype. Patient concerns A young Asian man presented with several years of progressive bilateral hearing loss followed by worsening dysphagia to solids and liquids, symmetrical limb weakness, muscle wasting, and acute-on-chronic dyspnea. Two siblings had previously died at a young age after developing a similar sequence of hearing impairment, dysphagia, limb weakness, and unexplained respiratory failure. Diagnoses Neurological examination showed tongue atrophy with fasciculations, thenar wasting, bifacial weakness, mild ptosis, diminished gag reflex, and symmetrical limb weakness. Audiometry confirmed profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Nerve conduction studies demonstrated predominantly motor axonal neuropathy, while electromyography showed chronic and active denervation. Repetitive nerve stimulation, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, magnetic resonance imaging, creatine kinase levels, and metabolic investigations were unrevealing. Targeted genetic testing detected pathogenic SLC52A3 variants, confirming RTD3/ Brown-Vialetto-Van Laere syndrome. Interventions High-dose oral riboflavin was initiated empirically at 40 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses before genetic confirmation because of progressive respiratory compromise and strong clinical suspicion. Supportive management included nutritional support and nocturnal noninvasive ventilation with bilevel positive airway pressure. Outcomes The patient showed marked improvement after riboflavin initiation. Respiratory effort improved within several days, and forced vital capacity increased from 35% to 50% of predicted within 1 week. Limb strength improved, and by 8 weeks the patient had gained 3 kg with stabilization of dysphagia and improved oral intake. At 6 months, neurological status remained stable without further electrophysiological progression. Riboflavin was well tolerated. Lessons RTD3 should be considered in young patients with progressive sensorineural hearing loss associated with bulbar dysfunction, motor neuropathy, or respiratory weakness, particularly when family history is suggestive. Recognition of the characteristic phenotype, targeted genetic testing, and prompt initiation of high-dose riboflavin may substantially alter the clinical course of this potentially treatable disorder.

Supportive management included nutritional support and nocturnal noninvasive ventilation with bilevel positive airway pressure.

Outcomes

The patient showed marked improvement after riboflavin initiation. Respiratory effort improved within several days, and forced vital capacity increased from 35% to 50% of predicted within 1 week. Limb strength improved, and by 8 weeks the patient had gained 3 kg with stabilization of dysphagia and improved oral intake. At 6 months, neurological status remained stable without further electrophysiological progression. Riboflavin was well tolerated.

Lessons

RTD3 should be considered in young patients with progressive sensorineural hearing loss associated with bulbar dysfunction, motor neuropathy, or respiratory weakness, particularly when family history is suggestive. Recognition of the characteristic phenotype, targeted genetic testing, and prompt initiation of high-dose riboflavin may substantially alter the clinical course of this potentially treatable disorder.

title: Concordance of p16 status between US-guided core needle biopsy and surgical specimens in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: A diagnostic accuracy study.
abstract: With the increasing prevalence of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), there is a need for efficient, minimally invasive methods to evaluate p16 status. This study aimed to assess the concordance of p16 status between ultrasound (US)-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) of cervical lymph nodes and surgical specimens, and to describe the numbers of CNB and surgical sessions required to establish the histopathologic diagnosis. This retrospective study included 39 patients diagnosed with OPSCC or head and neck squamous cell carcinoma of unknown primary (SCCUP) at a single tertiary hospital between March 2019 and March 2024. All included patients underwent US-guided CNB of cervical lymph nodes and a surgical procedure (biopsy or resection), and had evaluable p16 immunohistochemistry (IHC) results on both specimen types. The concordance rate for p16 status between US-guided CNB and surgical specimens was 100.0% (39/39; 95% CI, 91.0-100.0%; 35 p16-positive and 4 p16-negative cases). Sensitivity was 100.0% (35/35; 95% CI, 90.0-100.0%) and specificity was 100.0% (4/4; 95% CI, 39.8-100.0%). In all 39 included patients, a diagnosis of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma and an evaluable p16 result were obtained at the first CNB session. Among the 35 patients with OPSCC, 10 (28.6%) required more than 1 surgical session at the primary tumor site. No immediate complications were observed following US-guided CNB. In this cohort, US-guided CNB of cervical lymph nodes showed complete observed concordance with surgical specimens for p16 status, and a diagnosis with an evaluable p16 result was obtained at the first CNB session in all patients. Prospective, multicenter validation including more p16-negative cases is required before wider adoption.

title: Outcomes of sequential keratoplasty for bilateral gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy: A case report.
abstract: Rationale Gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy (GDLD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by subepithelial amyloid deposition, progressive corneal opacification, and recurrent erosions. GDLD may present during the first decade of life and interfere with visual development. It may recur after keratoplasty, complicating surgical management. Patient concerns A 21-year-old woman of Yemeni ancestry, living in a remote area with limited access to corneal transplantation, presented with progressive left eye visual decline and foreign body sensation since early childhood. She had long-standing bilateral visual impairment and a positive family history. Her first surgery was right eye penetrating keratoplasty (PK), performed elsewhere approximately 1 year earlier for an undiagnosed opacity. Diagnoses Examination revealed nystagmus, a clear right graft with yellowish recipient deposits, and dense limbus-to-limbus left corneal opacification with stromal haze, mulberry-like deposits, and neovascularization. Uncorrected visual acuity (VA) was 20/200 in the right eye and counting fingers in the left. Best spectacle-corrected VA was 20/100 in the right eye, while reliable refraction could not be obtained in the left. Histopathology demonstrated Congo red-positive subepithelial amyloid deposits with birefringence under polarized light, confirming GDLD. Genetic testing for tumor-associated calcium signal transducer 2 was not performed. Interventions The left eye underwent superficial keratectomy and attempted lamellar dissection assisted by intraoperative optical coherence tomography; dense deep stromal opacity necessitated conversion to full-thickness PK. Outcomes Both grafts remained clear without rejection during follow-up. Minimal focal subepithelial haze in a temporal area of the left donor graft was noted at the 2 most recent visits, remained stationary between them, and was clinically insignificant. At final follow-up, approximately 2 years after right eye PK and 10 months after left eye PK, best spectacle-corrected VA was 20/100 in the right eye and 20/80 - 1 in the left. Intraocular pressure was normal, and posterior pole examinations were unremarkable. Lessons Advanced bilateral GDLD poses clinical and surgical challenges. PK may restore corneal clarity and provide meaningful visual rehabilitation, although recovery may remain incomplete after early-onset visual impairment and delayed treatment. Long-term monitoring is essential because recurrence and repeat intervention may be required. Early recognition, timely referral, and individualized management matter where donor corneal tissue access is limited.

title: Bibliometric analysis and visualization of adenomyosis: From 1980-2024.
abstract: Objectives This bibliometric analysis systematically evaluated the research landscape, emerging trends, and key focus areas in adenomyosis to guide future research directions. Design Performance analysis combined with scientific mapping of global adenomyosis research literature. Data sources Web of Science Core Collection (1980-2024). Data extraction and synthesis Articles were manually screened. Bibliometrix (R 4.3.0), VOSviewer, and CiteSpace analyzed productivity, collaboration, citation patterns, and research trends. Derived data and analysis scripts are deposited in the Open Science Framework (OSF) under a citable DOI. Results Among 3100 included publications, China led output (752, 24.26%, full-counted), followed by the United States (414, 13.35%), Japan (350, 11.29%), Italy (215, 6.94%), and South Korea (128, 4.13%). In the 2 adenomyosis-specific corpora, however, the United States ranked first. The US had the highest citations and international collaboration, though international co-authorship among top-producing countries remained low (16.14%). Leading institutions were Fudan University (89), Shandong University (52), and University of Tokyo (49). Top journals by volume: Fertility and Sterility, Human Reproduction, and Journal of Minimally Invasive Gynecology. Research focus shifted from hysterectomy and uterine artery embolization toward high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU), and from endothelial nitric oxide synthase/induced adenomyosis toward ectopic endometrium. Eight keyword clusters emerged; the 4 largest (#0 EMT, #1 HIFU, #2 endometrial cancer, #3 pregnancy outcomes) form the present focus. Burst analysis identified "consensus" (2020-2024), "pathogenesis" (2022-2024), and "pregnancy outcome" (2022-2024) as recent and currently active hotspots. Conclusions Current adenomyosis research centers on ectopic endometrium and EMT in pathogenesis, fertility outcomes, long-term efficacy of HIFU and fertility-sparing surgery, links to endometrial cancer, and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Beyond deepening pathogenesis and pregnancy-outcome research, key future directions include enhancing international collaboration and developing internationally agreed, evidence-based standardized terminology, diagnostic criteria, and classification systems for adenomyosis.

title: Staged bilateral reverse sural artery flap reconstruction for severe frostbite of both feet in a patient with schizophrenia: A case report.
abstract: Rationale Bilateral, weight-bearing heel defects after frostbite are difficult to reconstruct, and outcomes depend heavily on postoperative off-loading and patient cooperation. We report a limb-salvage strategy for severe bilateral foot frostbite that occurred during acute psychosis in a patient diagnosed with schizophrenia. Patient concerns A 25-year-old man developed acute psychotic symptoms and walked barefoot in subzero conditions for about 12 hours, resulting in deep frostbite of both heels and multiple toes. During admission he had poor insight and repeatedly attempted weight bearing despite instructions. Diagnoses MRI/CT showed necrosis of the right first to third toes and bilateral posterior heel soft-tissue necrosis with preserved deep heel structures, supporting flap-based salvage rather than major amputation. Schizophrenia was diagnosed and treated concurrently. Interventions Reconstruction was staged. The right first to third toes were amputated, the right heel was debrided, and coverage was achieved with a reverse sural artery flap (RSAF). Three weeks later, the left great toe underwent debridement with split-thickness skin grafting, and the left heel defect was reconstructed with an RSAF. Strict positioning/off-loading and close multidisciplinary inpatient supervision were used to protect both flaps while psychiatric symptoms were stabilized. Outcomes At the last documented follow-up, 2 weeks after discharge - corresponding to 5 weeks after the left-sided reconstruction and approximately 8 weeks after the right-sided reconstruction - both flaps remained viable, with no total flap loss or flap-related reoperation, and small residual superficial wounds remained. No subsequent clinical follow-up was available. Lessons In frostbite patients with severe mental illness, reconstructive choice should balance technical "ideal" options against real-world feasibility. In this patient, staged regional flap reconstruction provided short-term wound coverage while accommodating psychiatric stabilization and limited adherence; however, long-term durability could not be assessed.

title: Relationship between extent of jeopardized myocardium derived from myocardial viability study to post-myocardial infarction outcome.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to assess the relationship between the extent of jeopardized myocardium, quantified using cardiac viability imaging, and clinical outcomes in patients after myocardial infarction. By utilizing rest myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) and cardiac 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) analyzed with Emory Cardiac Toolbox software (ECTb), the study aimed to determine how quantitative viability parameters correlate with left ventricular functional recovery and post-myocardial infarction outcomes, and to assess their utility in guiding clinical decision-making. Methods This prospective study included 85 patients who underwent 2-day rest MPI followed by cardiac FDG-PET/CT imaging. Quantitative parameters, including the percentage of jeopardized myocardium, comprising viable, scarred, and total jeopardized myocardial segments, along with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were obtained using the ECTb platform (version 4.2). The relationship between these quantitative PET parameters and functional myocardial recovery, defined as improvement in ≥5% LVEF as assessed by two-dimensional echocardiography, was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Follow-up was conducted over a period of 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year to assess the association between baseline quantitative imaging parameters and the occurrence of adverse cardiac events. Results The analysis demonstrated that the extent of viable myocardium was a strong predictor of functional recovery (area under the curve, 0.762; P < 0.001), with a cutoff of approximately 17% yielding 76.7% sensitivity, 68.8% specificity, and 71.8% accuracy. Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) occurred in 16% of patients. There was no significant association with imaging parameters, except a nonsignificant trend for scar burden in medically managed patients. Patients undergoing surgical intervention had a significantly greater extent of jeopardized myocardium, underscoring the role of viability imaging in therapeutic decision-making. Conclusion The extent of viable myocardium identified through imaging was strongly correlated with functional recovery, as reflected by improvements in cardiac function on follow-up echocardiography. Although no significant relationship with MACE was seen in the overall cohort, the higher burden of jeopardized myocardium in surgically treated patients underscores the value of viability imaging in guiding revascularization decisions, supporting FDG-PET/CT as a useful tool for post-myocardial infarction risk stratification and management.

title: The impact and value of [18F]-FDG PET-CT on management of patients with cervical cancer with service evaluation audited against national evidence-based PET-CT guidelines.
abstract: Purpose First, to assess the diagnostic value of fluorine-18-fluorodeoxyglucose PET-computed tomography ([18F]-FDG PET-CT) compared with conventional MRI and/or CT. Second, to audit the clinical indications for referring patients with cervical cancer for [18F]-FDG PET-CT against the 2022 guidelines published by the Royal College of Radiologists and the Royal College of Physicians. Finally, to evaluate the impact of [18F]-FDG PET-CT on management plans. Methods A retrospective cohort study of 49 patients with histologically proven cervical cancer across the Sussex Cancer Network underwent 59 [18F]-FDG PET-CT between 1 November 2020 and 31 October 2022. Scans were compared with the most recent CT and MRI scan conducted within 4 months of the [18F]-FDG PET-CT. Scan indications were categorized as either 'in accordance' or 'outside' the guidelines. Those in accordance fell into one of four groups: staging, response assessment, suspected recurrence, or staging when considering exenterative surgery. A questionnaire investigating the impact of the [18F]-FDG PET-CT on the management plan of each patient was answered by one clinical oncology consultant. Results [18F]-FDG PET-CT identified new metastatic sites in 16/59 (27.1%) scans. The remaining scans were concordant with the CT and MRI. The majority, 57/59 (96.6%), of the scans were performed in accordance with the guidelines. The management plan was changed by 5/59 scans (8.4%), confirmed by 48/59 (81.4%) and was not impacted with 6/59 (10.2%) scans. Conclusion [18F]-FDG PET-CT is superior to conventional imaging and enhances the management plan. Future cohort studies with larger patient numbers involving multicentric studies are needed to fully assess its impact on cervical cancer management and prognosis.

Those in accordance fell into one of four groups: staging, response assessment, suspected recurrence, or staging when considering exenterative surgery. A questionnaire investigating the impact of the [18F]-FDG PET-CT on the management plan of each patient was answered by one clinical oncology consultant.

Results

[18F]-FDG PET-CT identified new metastatic sites in 16/59 (27.1%) scans. The remaining scans were concordant with the CT and MRI. The majority, 57/59 (96.6%), of the scans were performed in accordance with the guidelines. The management plan was changed by 5/59 scans (8.4%), confirmed by 48/59 (81.4%) and was not impacted with 6/59 (10.2%) scans.

Conclusion

[18F]-FDG PET-CT is superior to conventional imaging and enhances the management plan. Future cohort studies with larger patient numbers involving multicentric studies are needed to fully assess its impact on cervical cancer management and prognosis.

title: Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review.
abstract: Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of carbonic anhydrase IX-targeted PET/CT for detection of clear cell renal cell carcinoma in patients with renal masses: a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies.
abstract: The preoperative differentiation of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) from other renal masses remains challenging. Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a highly specific target for noninvasive ccRCC imaging. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the diagnostic accuracy of CAIX-targeted PET/computed tomography (CT) for differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC renal masses. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Registers (up to 30 September 2025) was supplemented by a bibliographic review. Studies evaluating CAIX-PET/CT against histopathologically were included. Of 528 records, five studies (n = 544 patients) were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were synthesized using a univariate fixed-effects model; predictive values, likelihood ratios, and diagnostic odds ratio were also calculated. For the detection of histopathologically confirmed ccRCC (vs. non-ccRCC renal masses), the pooled sensitivity was 85.5% [95% confidence interval (CI): 81.6-88.7] and specificity of 86.5 (95% CI: 80.4-90.9). The hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic model yielded an area under the curve of 0.894. Exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a potential difference in diagnostic performance between the tracer subtypes. This review provides low-certainty evidence that CAIX-targeted PET/CT is a highly accurate, noninvasive tool for differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC renal masses in presurgical populations. Clinically, its high positive predictive value (94.6%) strongly 'rules in' disease, while its modest negative predictive value (~69%) limits its ability to 'rule out' malignancy. Further studies are warranted to validate these findings in broader clinical cohorts and for small-molecule agents.

title: Sleeve fractures of the patella: current concepts in diagnosis and surgical management.
abstract: Purpose of review Patella sleeve fractures are the most common patellar fracture in children yet remain frequently missed. Additionally, the options for their repair have grown. This review revisits how the injury is recognized and how the expanding range of fixation choices should be navigated. Recent findings Recent cohorts confirm that recognition rests on the examination rather than the radiograph, as the injury is frequently confused with Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome. In sleeve fractures that are displaced or minimally displaced and in which the extensor mechanism is disrupted, operative treatment is recommended. Transosseous suture remains the most common technique, with suture anchors used for smaller fragments. No fixation method has proven superior, as no comparative trials have been conducted in pediatrics. Functional outcomes are good across treatment groups. However, patients with operative injuries return to sport more slowly, and hardware removal is common. Summary Patient outcomes depend less on the choice of fixation than on timely recognition. A high index of suspicion and knowledge of this type of injury help facilitate an accurate diagnosis. MRI-confirmed chondral injury and fracture-specific repair yield reliable outcomes. A delayed diagnosis remains the principal avoidable cause of treatment failure.

Purpose of review

Patella sleeve fractures are the most common patellar fracture in children yet remain frequently missed. Additionally, the options for their repair have grown. This review revisits how the injury is recognized and how the expanding range of fixation choices should be navigated.

Recent findings

Recent cohorts confirm that recognition rests on the examination rather than the radiograph, as the injury is frequently confused with Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome. In sleeve fractures that are displaced or minimally displaced and in which the extensor mechanism is disrupted, operative treatment is recommended. Transosseous suture remains the most common technique, with suture anchors used for smaller fragments. No fixation method has proven superior, as no comparative trials have been conducted in pediatrics. Functional outcomes are good across treatment groups. However, patients with operative injuries return to sport more slowly, and hardware removal is common.

Summary

Patient outcomes depend less on the choice of fixation than on timely recognition. A high index of suspicion and knowledge of this type of injury help facilitate an accurate diagnosis. MRI-confirmed chondral injury and fracture-specific repair yield reliable outcomes. A delayed diagnosis remains the principal avoidable cause of treatment failure.

title: Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Abnormal Findings on Pre-Diagnostic Imaging in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Objectives Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is the third leading cause of cancer-related death. Although CT/MRI are used for initial evaluation, early imaging findings suggesting PDAC may be unappreciated, resulting in diagnostic delays. We aimed to determine the prevalence and types of pancreatic abnormalities on pre-diagnostic imaging in patients later diagnosed with PDAC. Methods We identified patients diagnosed with PDAC between 2022 and 2025 who had a pre-diagnostic abdominal CT/MRI performed 3-36 months before diagnostic imaging. These patients were compared with a non-PDAC cohort who underwent pancreas cancer screening but did not develop PDAC after 5 years of follow-up. The primary outcome was the prevalence and type of pancreatic abnormalities on pre-diagnostic scans. Results Among 733 PDAC patients, 151 (20.6%) had pre-diagnostic imaging (mean age 72.6 y, 53.6% F). At diagnosis, mean tumor size was 3.1 cm and 42.4% had metastatic disease. The mean (±SD) interval between pre-diagnostic and diagnostic scans was 15.9±9.5 months. Abnormal pancreaticobiliary findings were reported in 27.2% of pre-diagnostic scans. Pancreatic cyst prevalence was similar between pre-diagnostic and non-PDAC groups ( P =0.07). However, non-cyst pancreatic abnormalities were more frequent in PDAC pre-diagnostic scans ( P =0.04), including pancreatic duct dilation ( P =0.07) and pancreatic atrophy ( P =0.05). Conclusions Although >20% of PDAC patients had pre-diagnostic imaging, most pre-diagnostic scans reported no pancreatic abnormalities, despite eventual advanced disease at diagnosis. Subtle findings suggesting PDAC, such as duct dilation and pancreatic atrophy, were uncommon on pre-diagnostic scans but more frequent than in non-PDAC scans. These findings may represent early signs of PDAC and warrant closer surveillance.

title: Early Detection of Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Using Triple-phase contrast-enhanced Computed Tomography: A Case-control Study.
abstract: Objectives To investigate the imaging findings of the triple-phase computed tomography (CT), which was performed prior to definitive diagnoses in patients with Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Methods The single-center, retrospective, case-control study included patients with PDAC who underwent triple-phase CT 3-36 months prior to definitive diagnosis (pre-diagnostic CT) between January 2007 and March 2018 in Teine Keijinkai hospital. Triple-phase CT in sex- and age-matched patients without PDAC appearance in a 4:1 ratio were selected as controls. Findings were detected from each of the five divided pancreatic sections on pre-diagnostic CT by radiologists' reviews, and were analyzed by comparison with CT at the definitive diagnosis (diagnostic CT) to investigate risk ratios. Results Pre-diagnostic CTs were investigated in 190 and 760 sections with 38 PDAC and 152 control patients. In the diagnostic CT, 50 PDAC-positive and 900 negative sections were detected, respectively. In pre-diagnostic CT review, some findings were shown in 17 (34.0%) and 18 (2.0%) sections among PDAC-positive and negative sections, respectively, and the total number of findings was 46 and 28 in PDAC-positive and negative sections, respectively. Finally, different attenuation of pancreatic parenchyma in each phase, MPD stenosis, and focal pancreatic parenchymal atrophy were significantly correlated with the risk of PDAC. Conclusions While some findings may already appear on the pre-diagnostic CT in one-third of the PDAC-positive sections, an accurate and detailed review in triple-phase CT is indispensable to detect early PDAC in clinical practice.

title: Urolithiasis in Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia and Lymphoblastic Lymphoma (ALL/LLy): A Single-Center Case Series of Clinical, Metabolic, and Imaging Features.
abstract: Background Urolithiasis is an underrecognized complication in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (ALL/LLy), often associated with glucocorticoid therapy. Observations We report 4 cases of urolithiasis occurring at different diagnostic and treatment phases, 3 requiring intervention. Presenting symptoms included flank pain, hematuria, and urinary discomfort. In 1 case, renal abnormalities were incidentally identified on PET/CT performed for remission assessment. Conclusions Urolithiasis may occur across ALL/LLy diagnosis and treatment, particularly after glucocorticoid exposure and in patients with additional risk factors. Early recognition in patients with unexplained abdominal or urinary symptoms is essential to prevent complications.

title: Management of Monochorionic Twins: A Comprehensive Review of Major Guidelines.
abstract: Importance Monochorionic (MC) twin pregnancies are at risk of unique fetal and obstetric complications, which require increased surveillance and specific interventions to minimize the associated neonatal morbidity and mortality. Objective This review aimed to evaluate and compare the most recently published influential guidelines on the management of monochorionic twin pregnancies. Evidence acquisition A comparative review of guidelines from the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG), the Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada (SOGC), the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO), and the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynaecology (ISUOG) was carried out. Results All the reviewed guidelines recommend the determination of chorionicity and amnionicity in the first trimester, along with the precise labeling of the twins and confirmation of the gestational age based on the crown-rump length of the larger twin or the dates of assisted reproductive techniques. They also encourage the performance of aneuploidy screening during the first trimester, using either a combined nuchal translucency and biochemical markers test or cfDNA. A detailed anatomy scan is recommended, with emphasis on the fetal cardiac assessment. There is agreement on the recommended ultrasonographic surveillance protocol, the diagnostic criteria of TTTS, TAPS, and TRAP, the optimal timing of delivery in case of uncomplicated MC twins, and the need for earlier delivery in case of complications or MCMA twins. All the reviewed medical societies provide similar recommendations regarding the management of pregnancies complicated by TTTS, TAPS, discordant fetal anomaly, and demise of one co-twin. Minor discrepancies were identified regarding the diagnosis and management of sFGR, the routine assessment of cervical length, as well as the first-line aneuploidy screening method. Conclusions Multiple pregnancies pose significant maternal, fetal, and obstetric risks compared with singleton pregnancies, with MC twins being at the highest risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, particularly in the absence of increased surveillance or therapeutic interventions. The development and implementation of consistent international evidence-based practice guidelines for the prompt diagnosis and management of MC twin pregnancies and their associated complications may contribute to more favorable outcomes.

title: Radiographic union rate and predictors of nonunion after primary surgical implant generation network intramedullary nailing for open tibial shaft fractures at a major trauma center in Ethiopia.
abstract: Open tibial shaft fractures are a major source of morbidity in low- and middle-income countries, yet outcome data after Surgical Implant Generation Network (SIGN) intramedullary nailing (IMN) remain few. The study aimed to determine the radiographic union rate and identify predictors of nonunion after primary SIGN IMN for Gustilo-Anderson (GA) grade I through IIIA open tibial shaft fractures at a large trauma center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at AaBET Hospital, reviewing records and radiographs of patients treated between July 2016 and July 2022. Radiographic union was assessed at minimum 1 year using the Radiographic Union Scale for Tibial Fractures (RUST). Associations between clinical variables and union were analyzed with Fisher exact test, Mann-Whitney U test, and binary logistic regression. Eighty-seven patients met inclusion criteria (mean age 32.9 years; 86.2% male). Road traffic accidents accounted for 78.2% of injuries. The radiographic union rate was 89.7% (78 of 87). On multivariable analysis, GA grade IIIA (odds ratio [OR]: 36.2; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.21-90; P = 0.013), postoperative infection (OR: 20.2; 95% CI: 2.15-189; P = 0.023), and surgical delay beyond 48 hours (OR: 16.5; 95% CI: 1.88-144; P = 0.009) were independently associated with nonunion. Primary SIGN IMN yielded a high union rate for GA I to IIIA open tibial shaft fractures in this low- and middle-income countries setting. GA grade, postoperative infection, and delay to surgery were the principal barriers to union. These findings support early surgical intervention and rigorous infection control in resource-limited settings. Prognostic Level IV.

title: Sudden Unexpected Perinatal Death Due to Undiagnosed Diffuse Placental Chorioangiomatosis.
abstract: Chorioangiomatosis is a rare placental vascular disorder that may lead to severe fetal compromise and, in exceptional cases, sudden perinatal death. Its prenatal diagnosis remains challenging because diffuse lesions may lack a discrete placental mass and escape routine ultrasonographic detection. We report a case of sudden unexpected neonatal death occurring immediately after delivery following an apparently uncomplicated full-term pregnancy. External and macroscopic internal postmortem examinations were unremarkable. Histological evaluation revealed signs of chronic intrauterine hypoxia, while placental examination demonstrated diffuse chorioangiomatosis characterized by widespread capillary proliferation within immature chorionic villi and vascular wall hypertrophy. These findings supported a diagnosis of placental insufficiency leading to fatal hypoxia. This case highlights the critical role of placental histopathology in the forensic investigation of perinatal deaths, particularly when routine autopsy findings are negative. It also underscores the limitations of prenatal imaging in detecting diffuse placental vascular lesions. Recognition of this entity is essential to avoid misclassification of death and to ensure appropriate medico-legal assessment.

title: The 2026 World Health Organization Classification of Tumors of Soft Tissue and Bone: 6th Edition.
abstract: The 6th edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors (STB6) integrates the latest scientific and molecular discoveries with decades of pathological expertise to establish a globally accepted common language for diagnosis and clinical behavior. In this volume, the "essential" and "desirable" diagnostic criteria have been refined, considering different resource settings, ensuring accuracy while maintaining flexibility. A tumor type (entity) is a tumor in which multiple parameters (eg, clinical, histopathological, and/or genetic features) differ from those of other tumor types. In total, 19 new entities met these criteria and were added. A subtype is different in at least one dimension from the main tumor type (clinical, histopathological, or genetic), preferably resulting in a different treatment or outcome. A morphological pattern (no longer "variant") is important for pathologists to be aware of to facilitate recognition but is not associated with different clinical behavior. The classification was drafted by 203 editors and authors from 27 countries, representing genetics, medical oncology, surgical oncology, orthopedic surgery, and radiology, in addition to pathology. STB6 includes soft tissue tumors (n=116), bone tumors (n=46), vascular tumors of soft tissue and bone (n=18), undifferentiated spindle and round cell sarcomas (n=4), hematopoietic and dendritic cell neoplasms (n=6), and genetic syndromes (n=6). In total, 62 sarcomas are included. A consensus was reached among the expert editorial board. In this review, we highlight changes in tumor classification in STB6, including recently described tumor types, novel diagnostic markers, recent discoveries in molecular genetics, and improvements in prognostication.

title: Artificial Intelligence Segmentation In Musculoskeletal Ultrasound: A Novel Study Across Five Joints Using Expert Ground Truth.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the performance of an artificial intelligence (AI) technology in recognizing and segmenting anatomical structures across five joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist/hand, knee, and ankle/foot) in musculoskeletal ultrasound (US). Design This cross-sectional study included 79 adults. Software segmentations were compared to ground truth annotations provided by four experts. Performance was assessed using positive predictive agreement (PPA) and negative predictive agreement (NPA), with a true/false threshold defined as a dice similarity coefficient (DSC) ≥0.50. Subjects with and without sonographic disorders were evaluated to assess robustness. Results 3017 cine clips (15600 frames) covering 120 anatomical structures were analyzed. PPA and NPA exceeded 0.90 for most structures; tendons, muscles, and nerves showed near-perfect agreement (≥0.97). Similar performance was observed in healthy subjects (PPA: 0.93-0.96; NPA: 0.94-0.99) and subjects with sonographic disorders (PPA: 0.91-0.96; NPA: 0.91-0.99) (P<0.001). Conclusion This first large-scale study demonstrates the high accuracy and reliability of AI-based segmentation. By improving anatomical identification consistency during image acquisition, the software may help reduce technical operator dependency. The results further indicate strong potential for real-time assistance, supporting clinicians and trainees, and underscore the broader applicability of AI-based software in musculoskeletal US.

Objective

Subjects with and without sonographic disorders were evaluated to assess robustness.

This first large-scale study demonstrates the high accuracy and reliability of AI-based segmentation. By improving anatomical identification consistency during image acquisition, the software may help reduce technical operator dependency. The results further indicate strong potential for real-time assistance, supporting clinicians and trainees, and underscore the broader applicability of AI-based software in musculoskeletal US.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Ultrasound for Localizing Lymphovenous Anastomosis Sites in Lymphedema Surgery.
abstract: Background Preoperative vessel mapping is critical for successful lymphovenous anastomosis (LVA) in supermicrosurgical lymphedema treatment. Indocyanine green lymphography is common but limited by poor depth penetration and reduced visibility in advanced disease. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy, measurement agreement with intraoperative findings, and procedural efficiency of preoperative ultrasound in identifying surgically compatible LVA sites. Methods This study retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected data between April 2019 and January 2024 at a secondary care center. Consecutive patients with scintigraphically confirmed limb lymphedema underwent preoperative ultrasound to localize LVA sites, with intraoperative findings as the reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using positive predictive value (PPV), Bland-Altman analysis, multivariable logistic regression, and subgroup testing. Results Eighty-seven patients (mean age, 55.8 ± 12.8 years; 75 women) underwent 109 ultrasound examinations. Of 470 ultrasound-localized sites, 285 were selected for surgery; 272 were intraoperatively confirmed (PPV, 95.4%; 95% CI: 92.3, 97.5%). The 13 false positives were independent of tissue thickness, vessel size, depth, and distance (all p > 0.17). Ultrasound diameters showed minimal bias compared with intraoperative measurements [+0.13 mm (95% CI: 0.09, 0.17) for lymphatics; -0.10 mm (95% CI: -0.17, -0.04) for veins]. Mean total examination time was 34.7 ± 9.6 minutes; per-image analysis averaged 7.2 ± 2.3 minutes and was unrelated to diagnostic accuracy (p = 0.74). Conclusions Preoperative ultrasound enabled accurate, reproducible localization of LVA sites with strong anatomical agreement and consistent performance across participant and anatomical variables.

title: Comparison and Combination of Radiomics, Deep Learning, and Subjective Assessment for Differentiating Immature and Mature Ovarian Teratomas on Abdominal CT.
abstract: Objective Preoperatively, ovarian teratomas are often misclassified into immature and mature types, potentially resulting in adverse clinical outcomes. This study compared the diagnostic accuracy of radiomics-based machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and subjective radiologic assessment for differentiating immature from mature ovarian teratomas on abdominal computed tomography (CT) and evaluated whether combining these approaches improves discrimination. Methods We retrospectively reviewed imaging data of 31 cases with pathologically confirmed immature teratomas and 61 age- and size-matched cases of mature teratomas (mean age=18.1±9.2 y vs. 20.9±10.0 y). Two radiologists independently annotated predefined CT features to construct a multivariable logistic regression model. Radiomics features were extracted from precontrast CT with 3 masks: whole tumor, calcification, and fat. Radiomics models were developed using 4 ML pipelines (logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, and neural network). DL models were constructed with a 3D-ResNet18 on full-volume and tumor-segmented CT, with and without transfer learning (TL). A combined model was constructed by averaging their calibrated predicted probabilities. The diagnostic performance was assessed by the mean area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results In the full cohort, the 4 individual approaches performed similarly, with overlapping CIs: wavelet-transformed precontrast radiomics 0.820 (95% CI: 0.798-0.841), precontrast radiomics 0.817, subjective assessment 0.814, and DL 0.810. Combining them outperformed every individual approach (0.865; ΔAUC: 0.045, 95% CI: 0.032-0.060; Holm-adjusted P<0.001). Among the 81 tumors containing calcification, where calcification-mask radiomics could also be evaluated, all approaches performed better, and the combined model again outperformed each of them (0.891; ΔAUC: 0.035), as did the combined model among the 90 tumors containing fat (0.872; ΔAUC: 0.047; both P<0.001). Conclusion Radiomics shows moderate performance in CT-based discrimination between immature and mature ovarian teratomas, with subjective radiologic assessment and DL performing at a comparable level. Combining the 3 consistently outperformed anyone alone, indicating that quantitative image analysis complements rather than replaces expert visual interpretation and may help reduce preoperative misclassification.

Objective

Preoperatively, ovarian teratomas are often misclassified into immature and mature types, potentially resulting in adverse clinical outcomes. This study compared the diagnostic accuracy of radiomics-based machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and subjective radiologic assessment for differentiating immature from mature ovarian teratomas on abdominal computed tomography (CT) and evaluated whether combining these approaches improves discrimination.

Methods

We retrospectively reviewed imaging data of 31 cases with pathologically confirmed immature teratomas and 61 age- and size-matched cases of mature teratomas (mean age=18.1±9.2 y vs. 20.9±10.0 y). Two radiologists independently annotated predefined CT features to construct a multivariable logistic regression model. Radiomics features were extracted from precontrast CT with 3 masks: whole tumor, calcification, and fat. Radiomics models were developed using 4 ML pipelines (logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, and neural network). DL models were constructed with a 3D-ResNet18 on full-volume and tumor-segmented CT, with and without transfer learning (TL). A combined model was constructed by averaging their calibrated predicted probabilities. The diagnostic performance was assessed by the mean area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC).

Results

In the full cohort, the 4 individual approaches performed similarly, with overlapping CIs: wavelet-transformed precontrast radiomics 0.820 (95% CI: 0.798-0.841), precontrast radiomics 0.817, subjective assessment 0.814, and DL 0.810. Combining them outperformed every individual approach (0.865; ΔAUC: 0.045, 95% CI: 0.032-0.060; Holm-adjusted P<0.001). Among the 81 tumors containing calcification, where calcification-mask radiomics could also be evaluated, all approaches performed better, and the combined model again outperformed each of them (0.891; ΔAUC: 0.035), as did the combined model among the 90 tumors containing fat (0.872; ΔAUC: 0.047; both P<0.001).

Conclusion

Radiomics shows moderate performance in CT-based discrimination between immature and mature ovarian teratomas, with subjective radiologic assessment and DL performing at a comparable level. Combining the 3 consistently outperformed anyone alone, indicating that quantitative image analysis complements rather than replaces expert visual interpretation and may help reduce preoperative misclassification.

title: Whole-Body MRI of Inflammatory and Infectious Musculoskeletal Diseases: Emphasis on Chronic Nonbacterial Osteomyelitis and Systemic Inflammatory Disorders.
abstract: Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WBMRI) has emerged as the primary imaging tool for multifocal inflammatory and infectious musculoskeletal diseases. By extending coverage from the vertex to the toes in a single, radiation-free examination, WBMRI enables the detection of clinically occult lesions, disease-specific pattern recognition across bone marrow, joints, entheses, and muscles, and objective monitoring of disease activity and treatment response. This review describes the WBMRI findings-with detailed imaging features and distribution patterns-in chronic nonbacterial osteitis, SAPHO syndrome, seronegative spondyloarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, idiopathic inflammatory myopathies, and fever of unknown origin, with emphasis on validated quantitative scoring tools, disease-specific acquisition protocols, and structured reporting strategies for the practicing radiologist. WBMRI provides unique clinical value by mapping total lesion burden, supporting differential diagnosis, identifying biopsy targets, and tracking treatment response. Disease-specific protocols-tailored to the pathophysiological target of each condition-are essential for maximizing diagnostic yield. Quantitative scoring tools and advanced MRI sequences may improve the characterization of disease burden and longitudinal assessment.

title: Reduced Lumbar Lordosis in Fibromyalgia: Radiographic Evidence of Lumbar Straightening by L1-L5 Cobb Angle.
abstract: Background Reduced lumbar lordosis has been observed in patients with low back pain, but lumbar straightening has not been well characterized in fibromyalgia. We hypothesized that fibromyalgia would be associated with reduced lumbar curvature on standing radiographs. Objective To evaluate lumbar lordosis, quantified by the L1-L5 Cobb angle, in patients with fibromyalgia compared with patients with other rheumatic diseases and low back pain. Design Retrospective, cross-sectional observational study. Setting Rheumatology office practice. Participants A consecutive series of 245 patients aged 18 to 70 years who underwent lumbar spine radiography for moderate-to-severe low back pain between 2012 and 2014 was reviewed. Of these, 164 patients met American College of Rheumatology criteria for fibromyalgia and 81 met criteria for another rheumatic disease, including rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, or polymyalgia rheumatica. Intervention Not applicable. Main outcome measures Lumbar lordosis was measured on standing lateral lumbar spine radiographs using the Cobb angle between the superior endplate of L1 and inferior endplate of L5. The prevalence of a nearly straight lumbar spine, defined as a Cobb angle ≤10 degrees, and more complete straightening, defined as a Cobb angle ≤5 degrees, was also assessed. Results Mean L1-L5 Cobb angle was significantly lower in patients with fibromyalgia than in rheumatic disease controls (15.2±12.2 degrees vs. 23.3±13.4 degrees, respectively; p <0.001). A Cobb angle ≤10 degrees was present in 72 (44%) patients with fibromyalgia compared with 17 (21%) controls (p <0.001). A Cobb angle ≤5 degrees was present in 42 (26%) patients with fibromyalgia compared with 5 (6%) controls (p <0.001). Limitations The study was retrospective and conducted at a single site. Both groups consisted of patients referred for lumbar imaging because of low back pain, and no asymptomatic healthy control group was included. Potential confounding factors, including body mass index, age, sex, pain duration, and medication use, were not formally analyzed. Conclusion Patients with fibromyalgia had significantly reduced lumbar lordosis and a higher prevalence of near-complete lumbar straightening than patients with other rheumatic diseases referred for lumbar imaging due to low back pain. Because lumbar straightening was also present in the comparator group, it is not specific enough to serve as a standalone diagnostic sign. Lumbar lordotic straightening may represent an additional radiographic observation associated with fibromyalgia and warrants prospective investigation, including evaluation of its potential relationship with paraspinal muscle tension. Primary funding source This research was privately funded and received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. Trial registration Not applicable.

title: Metal Artifact Reduction in Lumbar Spine Instrumentation: A Comparison of Photon-Counting Detector-Computed Tomography Versus Energy-Integrating Detector-Computed Tomography, Iterative Metal Artifact Reduction, and Virtual Monoenergetic Imaging in 100 Examinations.
abstract: Objective Photon-counting detector (PCD) computed tomography (CT) systems allow the reconstruction of virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs) from inherently available spectral data. However, qualitative and quantitative evaluations of VMI in combination with tin-prefiltration (Sn) and iterative metal artifact reduction (iMAR), as well as their comparison to energy-integrating detector (EID) CT, are limited; therefore, the objective was to compare their performance qualitatively and quantitatively in the setting of lumbar spine instrumentation. Materials and methods Retrospectively, 100 clinical Sn CT scans after lumbar spine fusion surgery (50 EID and 50 PCD) were analyzed. Metal artifacts were quantitatively and qualitatively assessed in EID standard (EID std ), PCD standard (PCD std ), and PCD VMI at 120 keV (PCD VMI120 ), PCD iMAR (PCD iMAR ), and combined PCD VMI at 120 keV + iMAR (PCD VMI120+iMAR ). Regions of interest were placed in the most hyperdense and hypodense areas near metal artifacts, and the attenuation and SD/noise (SD) of Hounsfield Units (HU) were assessed as a quantitative artifact surrogate. For qualitative evaluation, 2 independent readers rated 6 image features on a 4-point Likert Scale. Results Seventy-four patients were included, of whom 26 underwent both an EID and a PCD CT. Radiation doses were significantly lower ( P < 0.01) for PCD CT [median CTDIvol of 6.4 mGy (4.6 to 8.4)] compared with EID CT [median CTDI vol of 12.5 mGy (11.1 to 13.7)]. Hypodense artifact attenuation was significantly reduced ( P < 0.01) with PCD iMAR (HU -260), PCD VMI120 (-176), and PCD VMI120+IMAR (-60) compared with EID std (-626). Hyperdense artifact attenuation was significantly reduced ( P < 0.01) in PCD VMI120 (HU 103) and PCD VMI120+IMAR (-1) compared with EID std (577). Qualitative artifact extent was rated significantly less severe in PCD iMAR and PCD VMI120+iMAR images compared with EID std ( P ≤ 0.01), while trabecular and cortical bone visibility was rated lower in PCD iMAR (2.73) and PCD VMI120 (2.63), P < 0.01, and lowest in PCD VMI120+iMAR (1.82) compared with EID std (3.19), P < 0.01. Significantly ( P < 0.01) more silhouette artifacts were present in the 100 kVp subgroup compared with the 140 kVp subgroup in PCD VMI120 and PCD VMI120+iMAR , and significantly ( P < 0.01) more dark zone artifacts in the PCD VMI120 series at 100 kVp compared with 140 kVp. Conclusion PCD CT with VMI 120 or iMAR achieved artifact reduction comparable to EID CT for lumbar spine metal artifact reduction, at nearly half the radiation dose. Combining VMI120 + iMAR provided the strongest qualitative and quantitative artifact reduction, but at the cost of the lowest cortical and trabecular bone visibility. 140 kVp acquisitions should be favored over 100 kVp acquisitions in PCD to reduce the occurrence of "dark zone" and "silhouette artifacts", suggesting a fixed tube voltage instead of an automatic tube voltage setting in instrumented lumbar spine imaging. VMI reconstruction of tin-filtered lumbar spine CT effectively reduces metal artifacts, with PCD favored over EID for its inherent spectral capabilities and the potential for substantial dose reduction.

title: Photon-counting Detector CT Spectral Reconstructions for Radiomics-based Liver Lesion Classification: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Objectives Accurate noninvasive classification of hepatic lesions remains a diagnostic challenge, particularly on conventional CT. Photon Counting Detector CT (PCD-CT) offers spectral imaging capabilities that may enhance tissue characterization. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of radiomics-based machine learning for differentiating benign and malignant liver lesions using multispectral virtual monochromatic and material decomposition images derived from contrast-enhanced PCD-CT. Materials and methods This multicenter study included patients with focal hepatic lesions, scanned on PCD-CT at 2 separate institutions. Lesions were automatically segmented by a nnU-Net model and confirmed by an abdominal radiologist. Volumetric segmentations were used to extract radiomic features from 9 spectral datasets: 40, 50, 70, 90, 110, 140, and 180 keV, virtual non-contrast (VNC), and iodine density maps (IDM). A patient-based classification analysis was conducted by training multiple machine-learning models, with lesion-level predictions aggregated per patient. A Random Forest model further evaluated classification performancef across all train-test reconstruction combinations. Results The cohort comprised 378 patients (median age: 62; 59.5% female) from 2 centers, including 190 benign (n=227 lesions) and 188 with malignant (n=2681 lesions) hepatic findings. Random forest model trained on VNC achieved highest performance [AUC: 0.899; 95% CI (0.840-0.951); Accuracy 83.5%). In the cross-domain analysis, all training reconstructions achieved similar mean AUCs (0.75 to 0.83). Evaluation performance varied across test levels. Models tested on 110, 140, and 180 keV, and VNC showed the highest stability (median AUC ≥ 0.83), while 40 keV, 50 keV, and IDM resulted in lower and more variable AUCs (median AUC ≤ 0.71). Conclusion Radiomics-based machine learning enables reliable differentiation between malignant and benign hepatic lesions on PCD-CT. The choice of test reconstruction influenced performance: higher energy levels and VNC images yielded more stable results. Incorporating high-energy reconstructions and VNC images into radiomic workflows for liver lesion risk stratification may enable noninvasive triage and reduce the need for invasive diagnostics.

title: Improved Visualization of Heart Valves With 4D-CT Using a Novel Motion Correction Algorithm.
abstract: Objective Motion artifacts remain a limitation of cardiac CT when assessing both native and prosthetic heart valves, particularly during phases of rapid motion. This may lead to reduced image quality, potentially impairing the evaluation of valvular movement and pathology. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether a novel reconstruction-based motion correction algorithm improves image quality and reduces motion artifacts of native and prosthetic heart valves compared with standard reconstructions in photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT). Materials and methods In this retrospective single-center study, 57 patients [21 women; median age, 71 (interquartile range, 57 to 78 y)] who underwent clinically indicated 4D cardiac CT for suspected native and prosthetic valvular disease were included. Images were acquired using retrospectively electrocardiography (ECG)-gated spiral dual-source PCD-CT without ECG-pulsing. Images were reconstructed in 10% steps throughout the RR-interval using both standard (TrueStack) and an otherwise identical reconstruction using the novel motion correction algorithm (ZeeFreePlus). Subjective image quality and motion artifacts were independently assessed by 2 blinded, experienced readers using a 4-point visual analog scale for 3 categories: valve frame/annulus, valve leaflets, and valvular pathology. Objective analysis included quantification of the volume of artifacts throughout the cardiac cycle. Results A total of 68 valves were evaluated, including 57 prosthetic valves (22 transcatheter aortic valve replacements and 19 surgical valves, 11 mitral valves, and 5 tricuspid valve interventions) and 11 native valves. Valvular pathology was present in 29 cases, with the most prevalent being hypoattenuated leaflet thickening in 14/29 (48%). Motion-corrected reconstructions significantly improved image quality and reduced motion artifacts across all cardiac phases and all categories (all, P<0.001). The largest improvements were observed during systole, particularly at 10% of the RR-interval, with significantly greater gains than during diastole (P<0.05). Improvements were consistent across aortic and atrioventricular prosthetic valves and translated into improved visualization of valvular pathology (P<0.001). Objective quantitative analysis corroborated the subjective image quality findings by demonstrating reductions in the volumes of motion-induced artifacts when using the algorithm (P<0.001). Conclusions A novel motion correction algorithm substantially reduced motion artifacts and improved image quality in both native and prosthetic heart valve imaging with PCD-CT, with the largest improvements in systole. These benefits resulted in enhanced visualization of valvular pathology, potentially reinforcing the growing clinical role of cardiac CT for the assessment of valve disease.

title: A Head-to-Head Comparison of Detection Rate and Tumor Uptake of FAPI, PSMA, and FDG PET/CT in Newly Diagnosed High-risk Prostate Cancer.
abstract: This study was designed to investigate the detection rate and tumor uptake of 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET/CT in newly diagnosed high-risk prostate cancer (PCa), compared with 68Ga-PSMA-11 and 18F-FDG PET/CT. This study enrolled 48 patients with biopsy-diagnosed, treatment-naive high-risk PCa who underwent 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, 68Ga-PSMA-11, and 18F-FDG PET/CT between April and December 2024. A head-to-head comparison of detection rate and tumor uptake was performed among the 3 tracers. In addition, 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68Ga-PSMA-11 dual-tracer PET was used to characterize the imaging phenotypes of each lesion and interlesional heterogeneity. A total of 477 lesions were detected by the 3 PET tracers. 68Ga-PSMA-11 exhibited the highest overall detection rate (96.4%), followed by 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI (81.1%) and 18F-FDG (66.0%). A total of 17 68Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions were identified in 8 patients, all of which were detected by 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, whereas only 12 were detected by 18F-FDG. Combined 68Ga-PSMA-11 and 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET identified all lesions detected by triple-tracer PET. Based on relative tracer dominance of dual-tracer PET, patients were classified as PSMA-dominant (n=23), FAPI-dominant (n=5), or mixed phenotype (n=20). The mixed phenotype with marked interlesional heterogeneity might be associated with more advanced clinical characteristics, with a higher proportion of metastatic disease and a greater metastatic burden. 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI is a promising PET tracer for newly diagnosed high-risk PCa. It may improve the detection rate of 68Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions and provide complementary information that could reflect interlesional heterogeneity. title: A Favorable Partial Response in Patients With Glioblastoma Multiforme Following Combined [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 and Chemotherapy.
abstract: This report highlights the potential role of [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 PET/CT in the early detection of active tumor recurrence in a 64-year-old woman with glioblastoma multiforme (IDH-wild type, WHO grade IV), preceding definitive radiologic evidence of disease progression. Following confirmation of recurrence, the patient underwent combined chemotherapy and [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 radioligand therapy, resulting in a favorable partial molecular and anatomic response as demonstrated by serial PET/CT and MRI examinations. This case illustrates the potential theranostic value of FAP-targeted imaging and radionuclide therapy in the management of recurrent glioblastoma.

title: Aortic Dissection Incidentally Detected on PET/CT During Evaluation for Suspected Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

title: FDG PET/CT Unmasking Acute Rheumatic Fever Presenting as Polyenthesitis.
abstract: A 13-year-old boy underwent FDG PET/CT to evaluate fever of unknown origin, which demonstrated extensive abnormal activity around joints of all 4 extremities and probable myopericarditis. Subsequent rheumatologic evaluation, including cardiac auscultation and echocardiography, identification of subcutaneous nodules, and elevated antistreptolysin O titers, established the diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever (ARF). Symmetrical polyarthritis with enthesitis-myotendinitis is an uncommon manifestation of ARF.

title: FAPI PET/CT Outperforms MRI and FDG PET/CT in Tumor Delineation for Low-grade Nasopharyngeal Papillary Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Low-grade nasopharyngeal papillary adenocarcinoma (LGNPPA) is a rare entity. We report a 27-year-old man with a 1-year history of bloody postnasal drip. MRI revealed a protuberance on the roof and posterior wall of the nasopharynx with contrast enhancement. 18F-FDG PET/CT showed mild uptake with poorly defined lesion extent, whereas 18F-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated intense uptake confined to the tumor with clear boundaries. No metastases were detected. Postoperative pathology confirmed LGNPPA, and the tumor boundary delineated on FAPI PET/CT precisely matched the pathologic extent. This case suggests that FAPI PET/CT may be superior to FDG PET/CT and MRI for tumor delineation in LGNPPA.

title: Sarcoid-like Reaction With Pleural Involvement After Neoadjuvant Chemo-immunotherapy For Lung Cancer: A Rare Mimic of Disease Progression.
abstract: We report a patient with stage IIA (cT2bN0M0) lung adenocarcinoma who developed new diffuse pleural, pulmonary, and nodal FDG uptake on 18FDG-PET/CT after three cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus cisplatin-pemetrexed, with slight regression of the primary tumour. These findings raised the diagnostic dilemma between disease progression and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-related sarcoid-like reaction (SLR). Rapid clinical and metabolic improvement after corticosteroid therapy supported SLR, which was subsequently confirmed histologically by noncaseating granulomas without viable tumour at surgery. This case highlights pleural involvement in SLR as a rare and diagnostically challenging immune-related adverse event.

title: FDG PET/CT in IgG4-related Disease Involving the Urethra.
abstract: Urethral involvement in IgG4-related disease is rare. We describe FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI findings in a woman with IgG4-related disease presenting as urethral wall thickening with obstructive urinary symptoms. FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI showed significant circumferential thickening of the urethral wall with intense diffuse activity (SUVmax, 13) and multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes in pelvic, retroperitoneal, mediastinal, pulmonary hilar, and axillary regions. This case indicates that IgG4-related urethral disease should be included in the differential diagnosis of FDG-avid urethral or periurethral lesions.
