title: Exceptional Thyroid Recurrence of Solitary Bone Plasmacytoma Detected by 18F-FDG PET/CT.
abstract: A 70-year-old man with prior occupational radiation exposure and a history of solitary bone plasmacytoma of the left hemipelvis treated with radiotherapy underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT for follow-up. Imaging revealed focal hypermetabolism in the right thyroid lobe, with no additional abnormalities detected. Ultrasound revealed an EU-TIRADS 5 nodule, and the cytologic analysis was indeterminate (Bethesda III). Core biopsy confirmed thyroid plasmacytoma. Although solitary bone plasmacytoma usually progresses to multiple myeloma, distant extramedullary relapse is uncommon. Thyroid involvement is exceedingly rare. This case highlights the value of 18F-FDG PET/CT and the need for histologic confirmation of suspicious thyroid lesions.

title: Not Every PSMA-Expressing Bone Lesion Is Prostate Cancer: Incidental Detection of Metastatic Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma on Staging 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT.
abstract: 68Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT is widely used for staging prostate cancer but may also detect nonprostatic malignancies owing to prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) expression in tumor neovasculature. Here, we report a case of a newly diagnosed high-risk prostate adenocarcinoma that underwent staging 68Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT. In addition to the primary prostatic lesion, PSMA-expressing lesions were identified in the sternum and right thyroid lobe. While skeletal involvement was initially presumed metastatic prostate cancer, further evaluation revealed follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma. This case highlights an important diagnostic pitfall and demonstrates the value of PSMA-PET/CT in uncovering clinically occult synchronous malignancies.

title: A Tale of 3 Tracers: Contrasting Uptake Patterns of 18F-FDG, 68Ga-DOTATATE, and 18F-MFBG in a Pediatric Neuroblastoma Patient.
abstract: A 5-year-old boy underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT before the histopathologic diagnosis of neuroblastoma, revealing a metabolically active left adrenal primary tumor with metastases to the liver. Following resection and chemotherapy, sequential 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and 18F-MFBG demonstrated tracer-specific uptake patterns: 18F-MFBG identified a solitary hepatic metastasis undetected by 68Ga-DOTATATE. This case underscores the complementary diagnostic value of multimodal molecular imaging in pediatric neuroblastoma response assessment.

title: [18F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Incidental Detection of a Benign Phyllodes Tumor in a Patient With Prior Colon Cancer.
abstract: We present [18F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT findings of an incidentally detected benign phyllodes tumor in a 68-year-old woman with prior colon cancer. Routine contrast-enhanced CT revealed a right breast nodule with moderate enhancement, and subsequent PET/CT demonstrated intense focal FAPI uptake (SUVmax: 6.63). Histology confirmed the presence of a benign phyllodes tumor. This case highlights that FAPI-avid lesions in cancer survivors may represent benign entities with fibroblast-rich stroma, underscoring the importance of considering benign diagnoses and obtaining histologic confirmation to avoid unnecessary treatment.

title: FDG PET/CT Combined With 3D CT Reconstruction in Diagnosing Inflammatory Granuloma Secondary to Fish Bone Perforation of the Ascending Colon.
abstract: A 71-year-old woman with a 5-week history of right-sided abdominal pain was initially suspected of hepatobiliary disorders. Upper abdominal ultrasound and MRI revealed unremarkable hepatobiliary findings. Although no hepatobiliary lesions were identified, MRI incidentally detected an ascending colon mass highly suspicious for malignancy. The patient underwent FDG PET/CT for differential diagnosis and preoperative staging. PET/CT with 3D CT reconstruction demonstrated a linear hyperdense foreign body within the ascending colon wall, causing focal bowel wall thickening with intense FDG avidity. These imaging findings were consistent with a foreign body-induced inflammatory granuloma, a diagnosis ultimately confirmed by colonoscopy and biopsy.

title: Chest Computed Tomography Manifestations of Legionella Pneumonia in a Large Multihospital Cohort of Immunocompromised and Immunocompetent Patients.
abstract: To assess chest computed tomography (CT) manifestations of Legionella pneumonia (LP) in a large, well-characterized immunocompetent and immunocompromised patient cohort. This retrospective study identified LP patients across a multicenter hospital system over 84-months. Chest CTs were reviewed for presence and distibution of ground-glass opacity (GGO), consolidation, and numerous other findings. CT findings were categorized into lobar, bronchopneumonia, atypical, and mixed patterns. Evolution on follow-up CT was assessed. 311/346 patients (median age 66.6 y [IQR: 55.9, 74.8]; 178 [57.2%] male) had CT examinations available. GGO (98.1%, 305/311) and consolidation (92%, 286/311) were the most prevalent findings, commonly coexisting. The segmental pattern occurred most frequently. The GGO and reverse halo signs occurred in 6.1% (19/311) and 3.5% (11/311), respectively. Follow-up CT occurred in 58.5% (182/311) (median=47.5 d), demonstrating improvement in 84.1% (153/182), worsening in 10.4% (19/182), stability in 5.5% (10/182), and new CT patterns in 12.6% (23/182). Respiratory co-infection occurred in 27.0% (84/311), commonly bacterial. title: Imaging Evaluation of the Transplant Liver.
abstract: Successful management of liver transplant recipients relies on accurate imaging evaluation of the liver allograft throughout the postoperative period. This review provides a practical multimodality approach to imaging evaluation of the transplant liver, highlighting the complementary roles of ultrasound with Doppler, contrast-enhanced ultrasound, multidetector computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging with magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, and selected nuclear medicine studies. Normal postoperative anatomy and expected imaging findings are reviewed, followed by a review of the characteristic imaging features of common vascular, biliary, and parenchymal complications. The strengths, limitations, and appropriate clinical applications of each imaging modality are discussed to facilitate accurate diagnosis and guide timely management.

title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of Blinded Lung Ultrasound and Clinicians in Pulmonary Consolidations: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Bedside lung ultrasound (LUS) is an increasingly utilized technique as an adjunct to clinical history and physical examination. This study aims to assess the added value of LUS by comparing the diagnostic accuracy of a blinded sonographer's ultrasound findings against the clinical suspicion of pulmonologists and emergency physicians at admission. A prospective single-center consecutive study of hospitalized patients (n=101) with imaging-detected consolidations was conducted. Ultrasound was performed by a blinded operator unaware of the physician's diagnostic suspicions. Definitive diagnoses were established through clinical-radiologic follow-up at 12 months, biopsy, and/or microbiological studies. The pulmonologist and emergency physician correctly estimated the probability of benignity/malignancy in 88.1% and 80% of the cases, respectively, whereas the blind operator achieved a 90% accuracy rate. Combining LUS findings with pulmonologists' clinical data improved benign/malignant classification accuracy to 96%. The agreement with the definitive dichotomous diagnosis (benign/malignant), assessed through Cohen kappa, was 0.664 for pulmonologists, 0.129 for emergency physicians, and 0.747 for the ultrasonographer. Ultrasound demonstrated a sensitivity (Se) of 85% and specificity (Spe) of 92% for diagnosing cancer. For pulmonologists, Se was 65% and Spe was 96%, whereas for emergency physicians, Se was 12% and Spe was 97%. The approach to hospitalized patients with imaging-detected consolidations that achieves the highest diagnostic accuracy (96%) combines clinical suspicion with ultrasound findings. Our findings confirm the importance of LUS, particularly in suspected malignancy.

title: Impact of Postbariatric Body Contouring Procedures on Patient Body Weight and Metabolism.
abstract: Background Bariatric surgery is an effective treatment that induces substantial and sustained weight loss through restriction, malabsorption, and hormonal mechanisms that regulate appetite and energy balance. This study aimed to assess the role of body contouring surgery in enhancing long-term weight loss maintenance and improving metabolic outcomes following bariatric surgery. Methods This prospective comparative study was conducted at Assiut University Hospitals on 60 postbariatric (sleeve) patients aged 20 to 60 years who underwent body contouring surgery and had been stable within 5 kg for 3 months. Patients were divided into 2 equal groups. Group A: underwent postbariatric body contouring. Group B: served as the control group and did not undergo body contouring surgery. Results Group A showed significantly greater reductions in weight at 3 months () and 6 months (), and in body mass index at 3 months and 6 months () than group B. A significantly lower basal metabolic rate was observed in group A at 6 months (), with a significant decline from baseline (). While hematological, coagulation, and B-type natriuretic peptide parameters remained comparable between groups, group A demonstrated significantly better metabolic and inflammatory outcomes, including lower total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels (), and higher high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels at 3 months and 6 months (). Furthermore, most patients reported high satisfaction with body contouring surgery. Conclusions Postbariatric body contouring surgery appears to be a safe and effective adjunct to bariatric surgery, contributing to sustained weight loss and improved metabolic outcomes.

title: Anatomy of the Upper Lip and Nose Muscular Bundle Tendon and Its Application During Unilateral Cleft Lip Repair.
abstract: Background While several authors have previously described the anatomy of the nasolabial muscles in patients with unilateral cleft lip, some personal intraoperative findings may provide additional information on this topic. The aim of this study is to describe the anatomy and histopathology of the tendon of the upper lip and nose muscle bundle on the cleft side and the role of myrtiform muscles during primary repair of the unilateral cleft lip. Methods The anatomy of this structure has been described during primary cleft lip repair, and small pieces of the muscle and tendon of the upper lip muscular bundle were excised and embedded in paraffin for histopathologic study. In addition, a retrospective cross-sectional study was performed to evaluate the utility of this anatomic structure in cleft lip and nose repair. The outcomes were anthropometric measurements of the repaired lip and nose at the age of 5 years. Results The anatomic descriptions during cleft lip repair and the histopathologic study confirm the existence of this tendon structure in all the studied cases. A well-defined tendon was detected at the base of the nasal ala on the cleft side. There was no statistically significant difference between cleft and noncleft alar base positions on the operated side in patients who underwent the described muscular repair. Conclusions A tendon structure has been documented and demonstrated in operated patients with unilateral cleft lip and palate nose deformity; it has not been previously described in the literature. The observed outcomes after primary cleft lip repair using this structure support its utility and underscore the importance of the myrtiform muscles during unilateral cleft lip repair.

title: What is the Utility of Whole Body Imaging for Screening Patients With Craniofacial Fibrous Dysplasia?
abstract: Whole body imaging is commonly performed in patients with fibrous dysplasia (FD) to screen for additional lesions. However, the frequency of newly-detected lesions in patients presenting with isolated craniofacial FD is unclear. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the frequency of newly-detected FD lesions on whole body imaging in patients with craniofacial FD and no known extracraniofacial lesions or symptoms. This was a retrospective observational cohort study at a tertiary children's hospital in an urban setting. The study population consisted of patients with craniofacial FD who underwent whole body imaging with technetium-99m (Tc-99m) bone scintigraphy or fluorine-18 sodium fluoride positron emission tomography/computed tomography (F-18 NaF PET/CT). Patients with previously identified extracraniofacial lesions, symptoms, or McCune-Albright syndrome were excluded. The primary outcome was the frequency of newly-detected extracraniofacial FD lesions. Fifteen subjects were included (80% female). Mean age at FD diagnosis was 9.6±4.3 years, and mean age at imaging was 10.4±4.2 years. Tc-99m bone scintigraphy was the most common imaging modality (86.7%). Newly-detected extracraniofacial FD lesions were observed in 1 of 15 subjects (6.7%). Two additional subjects (13.3%) had incidental skeletal findings related to recent traumatic injuries. In patients presumed to have isolated craniofacial FD, whole body imaging identified a low frequency of extracraniofacial skeletal lesions. These findings suggest that routine screening may be considered selectively based on clinical history and physical examination. Further investigation is required to develop evidence-based screening guidelines.

title: De-escalation of Axillary Surgery in Early Breast Cancer: Translating SOUND and INSEMA into Clinical Practice.
abstract: Objective To prospectively evaluate how often axillary staging can successfully be omitted in postmenopausal HR+/HER2- patients. Background Three randomized trials showed no difference in recurrence or survival outcomes with omission of sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) in cT1-T2N0 patients with a negative axillary ultrasound (AUS) undergoing breast-conserving surgery (BCS). We prospectively evaluated applicability of this approach. Methods From 3/1/24 to 9/1/25, SLNB was omitted in postmenopausal women age 50-70 years with unicentric or multifocal, clinical stage 1, grade 1/2, HR+/HER2- cancers and a normal AUS undergoing BCS. After the results of INSEMA were reported, tumors up to 2.5 cm were included. Patients with pathology showing grade 3, T≥3 cm, or HR- or HER2+ underwent multidisciplinary discussion regarding the need for SLNB. Results In 437 patients with 442 cancers, the median patient age was 63 years, median mammographic tumor size was 0.9 cm, and 74% were grade 2. A total of 34 patients (8%) had high-risk features on final pathology (grade 3, n=20; T≥3 cm, n=11; HER2+, n=3) and 14 (3.2%) had SLNB. Of these, 2 had SLN metastases. A total of 96% of patients received radiotherapy (40% whole breast, 56% partial breast), 415 (95%) received adjuvant endocrine therapy, and 31 (7%) received chemotherapy. At 7.7-month median follow-up, there have been no axillary recurrences. Conclusion Adoption of the SOUND, INSEMA, and BOOG 13-08 data allowed omission of SLNB in 97% of postmenopausal patients age ≤70 years with cT1-2N0, grade 1/2, HR+/HER2- cancers and a normal AUS, reducing the burden of treatment.

title: Accuracy of PET/CT for the Detection of Synchronous Malignant Lesions in Patients With Endoscopically Obstructive Colorectal Cancer.
abstract: Background This study aimed to assess the diagnostic performance of positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) in detecting synchronous malignant lesions in the proximal colon in endoscopically obstructive left-sided colorectal cancer. Materials and methods All patients with a biopsy-proven left-sided endoscopically obstructive colorectal cancer who had a preoperative PET/CT scan and a postoperative total colonoscopy within 6 months after the index surgery between January 2015 and July 2024 at a comprehensive cancer center were enrolled into the study. The synchronous malignant lesions on PET/CT were confirmed with the pathologic examination of the subtotal/total colectomy specimen and postoperative total colonoscopy. The primary endpoint was to evaluate the diagnostic performance of PET/CT in detecting synchronous malignant lesions, and the second endpoint was to determine the ability of PET/CT to distinguish malignant lesions from advanced adenomas. Results Out of 90 patients, 50 (55.6%) were male with a mean age of 62.46±10.81 years. title: Small Bowel Obstruction After TAPP Inguinal Hernia Repair: The Hidden Risk of Peritoneal Defects.
abstract: Background Small bowel obstruction following laparoscopic transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) inguinal hernia repair is rare and most often results from internal herniation through a peritoneal defect. Data describing its presentation and management are limited. This study aimed to characterize this complication. Methods A single-center retrospective study was conducted, including all patients who underwent elective laparoscopic TAPP inguinal hernia repair between January 2021 and January 2026. Patients who developed postoperative small bowel obstruction due to internal herniation through a peritoneal defect were identified. Clinical presentation, imaging, operative findings, and outcomes were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Results A total of 1927 unilateral and 531 bilateral repairs were performed. Five patients (0.2%) developed small bowel obstruction due to peritoneal defect herniation. All cases occurred after bilateral repair. Median age was 60 years (range: 37 to 77), and all patients were discharged on postoperative day 1 after an initially uneventful course. Most patients presented within the first few postoperative days with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting; one patient presented on day 23. Diagnosis was established by computed tomography in 4 cases and by clinical and abdominal x-ray findings in 1 patient. All patients underwent urgent laparoscopic exploration within 6 hours. The herniated bowel was reduced without resection, and the defect was closed laparoscopically. Median operative time was 49 minutes (range: 31 to 57). Recovery was uneventful, with a median hospital stay of 3 days (range: 2 to 4). At a median follow-up of 38 months (range: 2 to 62), no recurrence or readmissions were observed. Conclusions Small bowel obstruction due to internal herniation through a peritoneal defect is a rare but likely underreported and preventable complication after TAPP repair. It typically presents early after an initially uneventful course. Meticulous peritoneal closure may reduce risk. Early laparoscopic re-exploration is both diagnostic and therapeutic and is associated with excellent outcomes.

title: In older adults, "mild" by GCS does not mean low risk: Multicenter study of 1,157 patients with mild TBI and acute subdural hematoma.
abstract: Background Acute traumatic subdural hematoma (SDH) is the most common intracranial injury in mild TBI (mTBI), particularly in older adults. However, the relationship of patient and brain computed tomography (CT) characteristics with outcomes remains poorly described in a contemporary cohort. This study aims to characterize outcomes in younger and older adults with mTBI and isolated acute SDH. Methods This was a 10-center, retrospective cohort study of adult traumas with emergency department Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 13 to 15 and acute traumatic SDH on initial brain CT ('22-'23). Trauma registry, EHR, and Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) data were collected through automated and manual methods. The primary outcome was total mortality (TM=death+hospice discharge); the sample was stratified by 18 to 64 versus older than or equal to 65 years. Multivariable backward selection logistic regression examined 21 demographic, injury, and brain CT covariates. Results In total, 1,157 patients were included (18-64 y: 28%; ≥65 y: 72%; 58% transferred in). Median [IQR] non-head ISS was 1 [1-5] in 18 to 64 years, and 1 [1-2] in older than or equal to 65 years. Ten percent had neurosurgical intervention (18-64 y: 8%; ≥65 y: 11%). TM was higher in older than or equal to 65 years than 18 to 64 years (10% vs. 3%). Compared with older than or equal to 65 years, 18 to 64 years were discharged home more frequently (78% vs. 51%) and to hospice less frequently (2% vs. 7%). In 18 to 64 years, factors associated with TM were race, advance directive, functional dependence, ISS, more midline shift, and thicker SDH (too few TMs for adjusted models). In older than or equal to 65 years, factors independently associated with TM were advance directive (aOR [95% CI]: 11.8 [2.9-49.0]), male sex (3.0 [1.3-7.0]), midline shift (1.8 [1.3-2.6]), shock index (1.5 [1.1-2.1]), and worsening SDH on follow-up CT (2.9 [1.3-6.6]). Conclusions Despite presenting as "mild", these data highlight that older adults with SDH have high TM and should continue to receive the highest-level care with timely goals-of-care discussions. The association between advance directives and TM should be interpreted within the context of baseline vulnerability and preinjury treatment preferences, not as a biological mortality predictor. Level of evidence Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

title: Multicompartmental hemorrhage: A high-risk pattern associated with increased risk for progression in TBI patients.
abstract: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) with intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) often requires repeat head computed tomography (CT) imaging to monitor for bleed progression. While prior literature has explored patient-level factors, data on the impact of ICH morphologies (subdural [SDH], epidural [EDH], intraparenchymal [IPH], intraventricular [IVH], and multicompartment hemorrhage [MCH]) on radiographic ICH progression remains unclear. We hypothesized that MCH and IVH would have an increased associated risk of progression. Methods This retrospective (2021-2023) single-center cohort included adults (≥18 y) with TBI-related ICH who underwent initial and repeat head CT. Patients were stratified into radiographic progression versus no-progression cohorts, with progression defined as new or enlarging hemorrhage on attending radiologist interpretation of follow-up head CT. The primary outcome was the rate of radiographic progression for each ICH type. MCH was defined as the presence of two or more ICH types. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the association between each ICH type and radiographic progression, adjusting for age, mechanism of injury, Injury Severity Score, Glasgow Coma Scale on arrival, trauma-bay intubation, and preinjury antithrombotic exposure. Results Of the 817 patients with ICH on initial head CT and documented repeat CT, 401 (49.1%) had radiographic progression. Patients with progression were younger (58 vs. 62 y, p=0.027), more frequently male (71.3% vs. 63.7%, p=0.020), and had similar antithrombotic exposure (15.2% vs. 14.2%, p=0.678). Craniotomy/craniectomy was more frequent among those with progression (21.2% vs. 8.2%, p<0.001). On multivariable analysis, MCH demonstrated the strongest associated risk for progression (odds ratio [OR] 5.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.36-9.33, p<0.001), whereas IPH (OR 2.02, CI: 0.86-4.75, p=0.108), SDH, EDH, and IVH were not independently associated with radiographic ICH progression. Conclusions MCH was independently associated with radiographic ICH progression. This higher-risk hemorrhage pattern may warrant closer neurological monitoring. Level of evidence Prognostic/Epidemiologic; Level III.

title: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE).
abstract: Abstract Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) is one of the most common pediatric hip disorders and a frequent cause of diagnostic delay due to its variable and nonspecific presentation. Children often present with groin, thigh, or knee pain, gait abnormalities, or minor trauma, which can obscure early recognition. This case report describes a 10-year-old female who presented to an urgent care setting with hip, groin, and lower extremity pain following minor trauma and was diagnosed with SCFE based on physical examination and radiographic findings. Despite conservative pain management, persistent gait disturbance and limited range of motion prompted further evaluation, revealing posterior and caudal displacement of the proximal femoral epiphysis. This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for SCFE in pediatric patients with lower-extremity pain and gait abnormalities. Early diagnosis and prompt orthopedic referral are critical to preventing complications such as avascular necrosis, chondrolysis, and early-onset osteoarthritis.

title: Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 Reshapes Diagnostic Classification in a Real-World Memory Clinic Cohort.
abstract: Background Plasma phosphorylated tau-217 (ptau217) accurately identifies Alzheimer disease (AD), but its impact on real-world clinical diagnosis remains unclear. We evaluated the effect of plasma ptau217 on diagnostic reclassification in a memory disorders clinic. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 100 patients evaluated for memory impairment. Initial clinical diagnoses were established based on clinical evaluation, neuropsychological testing, and brain MRI without plasma biomarker results. Follow-up diagnoses were assigned after the availability of plasma ptau217 results. Diagnostic reclassification was assessed using binary (ptau217 > 0.18) and higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325) classification schemes. McNemar tests evaluated reclassification patterns, with subgroup analyses by apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 carrier status. Results Diagnosis reclassification occurred in 37.8% and 46.9% of patients using the lower and higher threshold, respectively (both P<0.001). With the higher threshold (ptau217 > 0.325), reclassification among APOE ε4 carriers was balanced (42% from AD to non-AD vs. 43% from non-AD to AD, P=0.096). In contrast, APOE ε4 noncarriers showed significantly greater reclassification from AD to non-AD than from non-AD to AD (66% vs.14%, P<0.001). Conclusions Plasma ptau217 meaningfully influences diagnostic decisions in memory clinic practice and may be particularly valuable for refining diagnoses among APOE ε4 noncarriers.

title: Novel therapies for glioblastoma.
abstract: Purpose of review Glioblastoma is the most aggressive and treatment-resistant primary brain tumor in adults. Given its clinical severity and biological complexity, research efforts are focused on understanding and targeting intratumoral heterogeneity, adaptive resistance, drug delivery barriers, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This review highlights emerging therapeutic approaches for the treatment of glioblastoma including advances in radiation planning, molecularly targeted therapy, immunotherapy, blood-brain barrier modulation, and neuronal signaling. Recent findings Radiation therapy remains a cornerstone of glioblastoma treatment, and advances in image-guided planning are being developed to refine treatment margins and improve tolerability without compromising efficacy. Blood-brain barrier permeability is being improved through device-assisted approaches, including focused ultrasound in combination with systemic therapies. Molecularly targeted and immunotherapeutic approaches continue to be evaluated, increasingly with biomarker-informed strategies to optimize patient selection. In parallel, drug repurposing, neuronal modulation, and metabolic interventions have shown promising preclinical and retrospective signals and are moving towards prospective studies. Interventions to improve quality of life are also underway with early palliative care showing significant impact for patients with glioblastoma. Summary As the field moves towards tailored and precision-guided approaches, combination strategies remain central to addressing the multiple mechanisms by which glioblastoma evades treatment.

title: AI-Driven Multimodal Risk Assessment Combining CT Imaging Biomarkers and Frailty Scores for Enhanced Mortality Prediction in Surgery Patients.
abstract: Background Automated frailty assessment predicts postoperative mortality, but routinely acquired CT imaging may provide complementary physiologic information. We evaluated whether AI-derived CT biomarkers improve one-year mortality prediction beyond an ICD-based Risk Analysis Index (RAI-ICD). Study design This retrospective cohort linked abdominopelvic CT scans obtained from 2013-2018 at a tertiary academic center to non-emergent surgery within 6 months. RAI-ICD was integrated with automated CT-derived muscle, adiposity, bone, and aortic calcification biomarkers using an XGBoost binary classification model, which we deemed the Unified Multimodal Model (UMM). The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality; discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve net benefit were evaluated. Results Among 7,672 patients, one-year mortality was 12.3%; 7,638 patients were included in primary mortality models. RAI-ICD alone achieved an AUROC of 0.75 and outperformed every individual imaging biomarker. Adding all imaging biomarkers increased AUROC to 0.79 (ΔAUROC +0.04; P<0.001). UMM calibration (slope 1.00; intercept 0.01; ICI 0.01) exceeded RAI-ICD calibration (slope 0.72; intercept 0.04; ICI 0.03), particularly at higher predicted risk. At the Youden-optimal threshold, UMM PPV was 0.24, NPV 0.96, and number needed to screen was 4.1. UMM provided significantly greater net benefit overall and among Robust, Frail, and Very Frail strata. Conclusions Integrating automated CT biomarkers with RAI-ICD improved one-year postoperative mortality prediction, high-risk calibration, and clinical net benefit compared with frailty assessment alone. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

Study design

This retrospective cohort linked abdominopelvic CT scans obtained from 2013-2018 at a tertiary academic center to non-emergent surgery within 6 months. RAI-ICD was integrated with automated CT-derived muscle, adiposity, bone, and aortic calcification biomarkers using an XGBoost binary classification model, which we deemed the Unified Multimodal Model (UMM). The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality; discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve net benefit were evaluated.

Results

Among 7,672 patients, one-year mortality was 12.3%; 7,638 patients were included in primary mortality models. RAI-ICD alone achieved an AUROC of 0.75 and outperformed every individual imaging biomarker. Adding all imaging biomarkers increased AUROC to 0.79 (ΔAUROC +0.04; P<0.001). UMM calibration (slope 1.00; intercept 0.01; ICI 0.01) exceeded RAI-ICD calibration (slope 0.72; intercept 0.04; ICI 0.03), particularly at higher predicted risk. At the Youden-optimal threshold, UMM PPV was 0.24, NPV 0.96, and number needed to screen was 4.1. UMM provided significantly greater net benefit overall and among Robust, Frail, and Very Frail strata.

Conclusions

Integrating automated CT biomarkers with RAI-ICD improved one-year postoperative mortality prediction, high-risk calibration, and clinical net benefit compared with frailty assessment alone. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: DeMorph: A Decoupled Deformation Model with Anatomical Guidance for Predicting Longitudinal Brain Atrophy.
abstract: Modeling the longitudinal progression of brain atrophy in Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is critical for early diagnosis and prognosis, but remains challenging for existing generative models. Current methods either fail to preserve anatomical integrity or treat progression as an entangled process, where changes from normal aging are inseparably fused with AD pathology. This fundamentally limits their scientific utility. To address this, we propose DeMorph, a novel deformation-based framework that explicitly disentangles and accurately predicts longitudinal brain MRI changes. Our transformer-based architecture features two key innovations: (1) a Decoupled Feed-Forward Network (D-FFN) for separate aging and pathology deformation pathways; and (2) a Multi-Scale Anatomical Guidance Cross-Attention (MS-AGCA) module, which explicitly injects anatomical priors to ensure spatially precise and biologically plausible disentanglement. Extensive experiments on four datasets (ADNI, OASIS-3, AIBL, and an inhouse dataset) demonstrate that DeMorph achieves stateof- the-art performance in both image similarity and anatomical accuracy. Crucially, we validate the success of our framework through robust bidirectional counterfactual synthesis, demonstrating the ability to controllably induce and remove a quantitatively plausible, AD-specific pathological effect.

title: VL-AcneSeg: A Vision-Language Framework for Region-Aware Acne Lesion Segmentation.
abstract: Acne assessment is crucial for clinical decision-making, yet traditional grading and counting are subjective and fail to account for lesion size. While areabased assessment has emerged as a promising alternative, acne segmentation has continued to rely on generalpurpose architectures. To address this gap, we propose VLAcneSeg, a multimodal framework for acne lesion segmentation that leverages CLIP and region-level text prompts to incorporate spatial priors, enabling lesions to be localized across the whole face. Because region-level prompts indicate which facial areas contain lesions, we report a single global prompt, which requires no such information, as our primary setting. On our internal clinical dataset, VLAcneSeg achieves a Dice score of 0.5082 and an IoU of 0.3407 under this protocol, the highest among all compared methods, including recent vision-language segmentation methods that are themselves given region-level prompts; region-level prompting raises these to 0.5296 and 0.3602. Moreover, lesion area measurements derived from our segmentation correlate with IGA scores at a level comparable to expert annotations (Pearson r = 0.719 versus 0.658). Notably, our framework maintains consistent performance across external validation datasets, performing reliably even on uncontrolled smartphone images without requiring additional training or fine-tuning. By pairing a protocol that requires no lesion-location information with area-based severity estimation, this work provides a foundation for objective acne assessment outside the clinic.

title: Imaging Informatics for Thermal Ablation: CT Thermometry-Based Tissue Injury Mapping.
abstract: Sparse CT acquisition during CT-guided thermal ablation limits direct estimation of cumulative ther mal injury, which depends on temperature history rather than endpoint temperature alone. This study developed an imaging-informatics pipeline for near real-time Arrhenius injury mapping from workflow-compatible endpoint CT thermometry. Endpoint temperature fields were derived from ROI-level HU-temperature calibration and deployed in baseline-referenced form. Protocol-specific normalized temperature-history templates reconstructed heating trajectories at 180 and 300 s, and precompiled endpoint temperature-to-logΩ mappings avoided voxel-wise temporal integration at runtime. Validation was limited to ex vivo liver specimens, using porcine tissue for model de velopment and validation and two bovine cases for ex ploratory cross-tissue evaluation. Across five indepen dent experiments, per-update latency was 793.7-1688.0 ms (1198.5±434.3 ms). The logΩ ≥ 0 delineation yielded mean absolute major- and minor-axis errors of 0.96±0.73 mm and 1.98 ± 1.37 mm, respectively, with Dice 0.9151 ± 0.0311 and HD952.07±0.27 mmrelative to gross specimen boundaries. Dice and HD95 quantify post-alignment two-dimensional contour agreement after scale normalization rather than absolute localization accuracy. Leakage-controlled calibration analysis indicated limited out-of-sample CT thermometry performance, whereas two-level validation supported the stability of the endpoint-temperature-to-injury mapping. These ex vivo results demonstrate protocol-specific feasibility and motivate independent thermometry validation, uncertainty propagation, and prospective in vivo evaluation.

title: TEAM: Text-Augmented Medical Image Segmentation with Entity-Level Modal Alignment and Masked Modeling.
abstract: Text-augmented medical image segmentation has become a promising approach to improving medical image analysis by incorporating linguistic descriptions into dense prediction, especially for identifying and segmenting complex anatomical structures. However, existing methods often face challenges due to the semantic gap between concise textual descriptions and dense visual context. This would easily cause the over-alignment or under-alignment issues, resulting in suboptimal segmentation performance. In this paper, we propose a novel framework named TEAM to improve the alignment between visual and textual features and mitigate the potential over-alignment and under-alignment problems. Specifically, our approach introduces an entity contrastive learning (ECL) strategy to enhance the fine-grained correspondence between textual and visual features at their semantic entity levels. In addition, we develop the vision-language feature reconstruction (VL-R) module, which combines masked vision modeling (MVM) with masked latent language modeling (MLM) to further strengthen multimodal feature alignment while preserving the critical and discriminative visual features for precise segmentation. Evaluated on the QaTa-COV19, MosMedData+, and Kvasir-SEG benchmarks, our framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Extensive ablation studies and qualitative visualizations further confirm the effectiveness of our design in enhancing cross-modal alignment and segmentation accuracy, highlighting its potential as a robust solution for text-augmented medical image segmentation.

title: SGF-RWKV: Semantic-Guided and Frequency-Enhanced RWKV for Unified Medical Image Denoising.
abstract: Medical image denoising is essential for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and clinical applicability. Since diverse imaging modalities exhibit heterogeneous noise characteristics, developing a unified all-in-one frame work is critical to avoid modality-specific solutions and improve generalization. However, existing approaches struggle with three key challenges: difficulty in uniformly modeling multimodal noise, loss of structural details, and limited spatial context modeling. To addressthis issue, wepropose SGF-RWKV, a unified medical image denoising framework built upon the Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) model for consistent noise modeling across modalities. Specifically, a semantic guided module leverages CLIP based language embeddings to generate task-aware attention maps for adaptive noise suppression, a frequency enhancement module refines structural and edge details via Fourier magnitude modeling, and a dilated multi-scale shift mechanism extends spatial context modeling to preserve continuity and fine texture. By jointly integrating semantic, frequency, and spatial cues, SGF-RWKV achieves modality agnostic denoising within a unified framework. We con ducted comprehensive experiments on five publicly available medical imaging datasets spanning multiple modalities, including MRI, CT, ultrasound, OCT, and cryo-EM. Experimental results demonstrate that our unified denoising framework achieves superior performance across diverse medical imaging modalities, excelling in key quantitative metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and RMSE. The source code is available at https://github.com/zwj666a/SGF_RWKV.

title: TwinFedSeg: Anatomical Twin State-Guided Federated Learning for Multimodal Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Federated learning enables privacy-preserving collaborative healthcare, while digital twins can represent institution-specific anatomical and modality states. However, federated multimodal medical image segmentation remains challenged by cross-center heterogeneity and missing modalities, while existing methods largely overlook the anatomical and modality complementarity of client updates. To address this problem, we propose TwinFedSeg, a federated learning framework guided by an anatomical twin state for multimodal medical image segmentation. Each client maintains a lightweight state comprising dynamic class prototypes, structural statistics, modality availability, and reliability. These states guide client selection, model aggregation, and global state updating, while the updated global state is fed back through a lightweight feature modulation adapter for cross-center adaptation under missing modalities. Extensive experiments on BraTS 2023-GLi and ISLES 2022 show that TwinFedSeg consistently outperforms representative federated methods, achieving average Dice scores of 80.77% and 72.58%, respectively, with gains of 3.52 and 4.06 percentage points over FedAvg.

title: DINOSAM+: Structure-Guided Prompt Learning for Semi-Supervised 3D Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Semi-supervised 3D medical image segmentation under low-label settings often suffers from noisy pseudo labels and anatomically inconsistent predictions, which limit segmentation reliability. Existing methods primarily emphasize training strategies or loss engineering, but they still fail to sufficiently exploit structural priors to guide pseudo-label generation and unlabeled supervision. Hence, we propose DINOSAM+, a structure-guided semi-supervised framework for reliable 3D medical image segmentation. Specifically, a frozen self-supervised representation model, DINOv2, is employed to extract coarse structural attention from volumetric slices, which is further refined by a lightweight structure-aware network into foreground, boundary, and background probability maps, thereby providing more discriminative structural cues for pseudo-label generation. Based on these refined structural maps, structure-aware prompts are automatically generated for SAM-Med3D to produce pseudo labels with improved spatial consistency and structural completeness. The resulting pseudo labels are then incorporated into a Mean Teacher framework with confidence filtering, improving the reliability of unlabeled supervision and reducing error accumulation during training. Experiments on the LA and Synapse datasets show improved Dice, HD95, and worst-case performance under limited annotations.

title: Unsupervised CT Metal Artifact Reduction Via Consistent Artifact Modeling.
abstract: Metal artifacts severely corrupt CT images, masking anatomical structures and undermining diagnostic reliability. Although supervised metal artifact reduction (MAR) achieves strong suppression, its dependence on paired clean and corrupted data confines it to simulated domains and hinders clinical translation. We recast unsupervised MAR as an artifact-consistent residual learning problem and propose a physically grounded, attention-guided generative framework that closes the loop between artifact estimation and removal. A single-generator dual-branch architecture estimates metal-induced corruption as a transferable additive residual and reinjects it to synthesize controlled degraded samples during cyclic training, explicitly constraining the removable component. Guided by interpolated pseudo-priors, a difference-aware attention mechanism concentrates correction on corrupted regions while safeguarding intact anatomy, all without paired supervision. Extensive experiments on synthetic benchmarks and real clinical data show that our method restores structural fidelity, suppresses streaks and beam-hardening, and generalizes robustly across diverse implants and anatomical sites. Beyond perceptual quality, it delivers state-of-the-art pelvic bone segmentation under metal corruption at efficient inference cost. This work charts an interpretable, efficient, and clinically scalable route toward reliable CT metal artifact suppression in real-world practice. Our source code is available at https://github.com/wonderfulpoet/CAM-Net.

title: EndoCADx: A Preference-Aligned Vision-Language Framework for Standardized Descriptive Diagnosis in Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy.
abstract: The subjective nature of descriptive endoscopic diagnosis and the propensity of large vision-language models (LVLMs) to produce semantic hallucinations pose significant threats to clinical safety and standardized patient management. While computer-aided detection (CADe) systems are widely adopted for lesion localization, the transition toward standardized descriptive diagnosis (CADx) remains hindered by large model size, high inference latency, and hallucination risks. To address these barriers, we propose EndoCADx, a compact, low-latency generative framework tailored for standardized gastric descriptive diagnosis. We formalize a two-stage optimization pipeline comprising domain-specific supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and error-driven Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). By systematically mining failure-mode subsets from the initial SFT baseline, we perform targeted recalibration of the model's latent policy to improve concordance between generated descriptions and expert reference annotations. EndoCADx provides an on-demand response time of 1.46 s per physician-selected frozen keyframe, compatible with the routine "freeze-and-inspect" workflow. Extensive evaluation on EndoGastro-500, a multi-center independent cohort from six heterogeneous clinical centers, demonstrates robust performance: the DPO-aligned model achieves 91.6% Lesion Recognition Accuracy (ALR) and 84.7% Feature Description Accuracy (AFD), with the latter reflecting improved attribute-level consistency with expert annotations. A comprehensive Multi-Reader, Multi-Case (MRMC) study involving 12 endoscopists further reveals that EndoCADx acts as a standardizing agent; while conventional CADe alone yields only moderate inter-rater reliability (Kappa = 0.64), EndoCADx elevates diagnostic consistency to almost perfect agreement (Kappa = 0.88), particularly benefiting novice clinicians with a 17.20% accuracy gain. By balancing real-time efficiency with expert-aligned safety, this work offers a practical paradigm for the clinical translation of endoscopic VLMs as a reliable supplementary aid to professional judgment.

title: FlowPredictor-Corrector: A Hemodynamics-Guided Two-Step Deep Learning Framework for Vascular Flow Prediction.
abstract: Accurate hemodynamic assessment is of significant clinical value in the diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. However, obtaining noninvasive, rapid, and high-fidelity hemodynamic information remains challenging. Invasive measurements carry risks, numerical simulations rely on complex modeling and high computational power, and while deep learning methods are efficient, they often lack physical constraints, leading to unstable performance in complex and diverse vascular geometries. To address this, we propose an innovative two-step framework called FlowPredictor-Corrector (FPC), which integrates point-cloud learning with physics-based hemodynamic correction to achieve a rapid mapping from vascular geometry to 4D hemodynamics. We constructed a dataset across three carotid artery anatomical regions (normal ICA C1 segment, normal carotid bifurcation, and stenotic carotid bifurcation) and conducted a systematic comparison with mainstream point cloud models (PointNet, PointNet++, Point Transformer). Our results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high consistency with reference data for hemodynamic predictions ($R^{2} > 0.92$). Furthermore, it shows high agreement with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and clinical ultrasound reports in stenotic grade classification based on internal carotid artery (ICA)/common carotid artery (CCA) peak systolic velocity (PSV) ($AUC = 0.947$). The model inference time was approximately 1.0 s per case. In summary, FPC not only balances efficiency with accuracy but also exhibits strong physical consistency and clinical interpretability, supporting further investigation toward rapid 4D hemodynamic prediction and potential clinical applications. To facilitate reproducibility and further research, the code and a representative test case are publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/FPC-B09E.

Our results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high consistency with reference data for hemodynamic predictions ($R^{2} > 0.92$). Furthermore, it shows high agreement with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and clinical ultrasound reports in stenotic grade classification based on internal carotid artery (ICA)/common carotid artery (CCA) peak systolic velocity (PSV) ($AUC = 0.947$). The model inference time was approximately 1.0 s per case. In summary, FPC not only balances efficiency with accuracy but also exhibits strong physical consistency and clinical interpretability, supporting further investigation toward rapid 4D hemodynamic prediction and potential clinical applications. To facilitate reproducibility and further research, the code and a representative test case are publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/FPC-B09E.

title: Hierarchical Vision Transformer with Prototypes for Interpretable Medical Image Classification.
abstract: Explainability is an important requirement for machine learning models in high-risk domains such as medicine. We introduce HierViT, a hierarchical Vision Transformer that combines competitive predictive performance with multiple mechanisms to support the interpretation of its predictions. The model first predicts clinically relevant visual appearance attributes, which are then used to infer the final target prediction through a hierarchical reasoning process. To facilitate understanding of the intermediate representations, attribute-specific prototypes are visualized as representative image examples, while attribute-specific attention maps highlight image regions associated with each visual feature. Together, these attribute-level components provide complementary views of the model's reasoning by linking representative image examples and spatial attention to semantically defined visual features. We evaluate HierViT on two medical benchmark datasets: LIDC-IDRI for lung nodule assessment and derm7pt for skin lesion classification. Across both datasets, HierViT achieves competitive predictive performance while providing attribute-level prototypes and attention visualizations that support the interpretation of its predictions.

title: Anatomical-Persistent Synergy Mamba for Joint Pre-to-Postoperative CT Synthesis and Multi-structure Segmentation in Orbital Decompression Surgery.
abstract: Thyroid Eye Disease (TED) often causes proptosis and optic nerve compression, and orbital decompression surgery is commonly performed to relieve these symptoms. However, postoperative anatomical changes are highly nonlinear and patient-specific due to bone removal and orbital content displacement, which makes reliable preoperative prediction both critical and challenging. Existing methods for pre- to postoperative medical image generation often overlook an important clinical prior that, although surgery induces local structural changes, the overall anatomy of the same patient remains largely consistent, and neglecting this can lead to anatomically implausible deviations. To address this issue, we propose APS-Mamba (Anatomical-Persistent Synergy Mamba), a conditional multi-task framework that takes preoperative CT and surgical information as input and jointly performs postoperative CT synthesis and multi-structure segmentation. The model introduces an anatomical persistence constraint to preserve structural consistency in non-operated regions while allowing realistic local deformations in surgery-related areas. It also incorporates a generation-segmentation synergistic learning strategy. In this design, morphological image synthesis provides predicted variations for segmentation, and segmentation enforces semantic constraints to improve the structural fidelity of generated images. Experiments on a clinical TED dataset demonstrate that APS-Mamba outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both image synthesis (PSNR 28.60 dB, SSIM 91.72%) and segmentation (mean DSC 86.17%). Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the anatomical constraint and synergistic learning strategy in modeling anatomical changes.

title: Q-LCAN: Anatomy-Constrained Quantum-Agentic Systems for MRI-Derived Structural Surgical Digital Twins in Uterine Adenomyosis.
abstract: Accurate patient-specific structural assessment of adenomyosis is essential for fertility-preserving treatment planning, but pelvic T2-weighted MRI is difficult to parse because the uterus, endometrium, ectopic glands, hemorrhagic foci, and adenomyoma are nested, overlapping, and highly imbalanced. We propose Q-LCAN, an anatomy-constrained Quantum-Agentic System that converts MRI into a structured surgical digital twin. A dense 3D decoder first estimates target-specific probability maps and signed distance fields. Five target agents then exchange visual evidence under predefined anatomical axioms, while quantum-enhanced differentiable action projection (Q-DAP) calibrates restricted expand, shrink, or hold actions before vision-language level-set control. A detached anatomical correction module and an independent audit reduce and report residual violations. On 658 multicenter examinations, Q-LCAN achieved case-level five-target macro-average DSC/ASSD of 0.814/2.23 mm in internal five-fold validation and 0.802/2.33 mm in external testing. Compared with the strongest protocol-aligned baseline, Q-LCAN improved macro DSC by 0.018 and 0.019 and reduced ASSD by 0.29 and 0.31 mm, with gains concentrated in ectopic glands, hemorrhagic foci, adenomyoma burden, lesion-to-endometrium distance, residual lesion ratio, and candidate resection-boundary distance. Q-LCAN provides an auditable quantum-agentic framework for MRI-derived structural twins; its millimeter-scale descriptors are intended as preoperative decision support, not autonomous operative guidance.

title: Adaptive Control Point B-Spline Method for Improving Accuracy and Deformation Plausibility in Deep Learning Brain Registration.
abstract: Deformable brain image registration plays a crucial role in aligning and jointly analyzing multi-phase and multi-modal neuroimaging data. However, existing unsupervised deep learning-based registration methods typically predict dense displacement fields directly at the voxel level, which often leads to deformation noise and optimization difficulties due to redundant degrees of freedom. Furthermore, these methods are prone to topological distortions when noise or irrelevant information is present. To address these challenges, we propose a robust B-spline registration post-processing framework with adaptive control point density, which can be seamlessly integrated into mainstream registration architectures for brain analysis. Specifically, we design a Control Point Spacing Predictor (CPSPredictor) that adaptively adjusts the distribution density of control points based on the input images, enabling effective regulation of registration flexibility. By modeling displacements with sparse control points and generating continuous and smooth deformation fields via locally supported B-spline basis functions, the proposed method significantly suppresses folding artifacts and preserves anatomical consistency. Extensive experiments on multiple publicly available brain MRI datasets demonstrate that our approach can be seamlessly integrated into existing mainstream registration frameworks, significantly improving both registration accuracy and the physical plausibility of the transformation. For instance, on the IXI dataset, our method boosts the VoxelMorph baseline's DSC by 2.63% and reduces the number of folding points nearly 69-fold. The resulting registration outputs better align with clinical diagnostic requirements, highlighting the method's robustness and practical application potential.

title: ScanSeg: Policy-Guided Sequential Prompting for Dense Fine-Grained Ultrasound Segmentation.
abstract: Dense fine-grained segmentation on standardized ultrasound planes is clinically essential but remains challenging because multiple anatomical structures coexist under speckle noise, acoustic shadowing, weak boundaries, and partial visibility. Promptable foundation models can produce high-quality masks when queried, but they typically return one structure at a time and lack a mechanism to automatically decide what to segment next and where additional evidence is needed, making single-shot "auto" outputs brittle on complex planes. This paper introduces ScanSeg, a scan-inspired framework that formulates multi-structure ultrasound segmentation as sequential evidence accumulation via a small number of prompted calls. ScanSeg maintains a global per-pixel posterior over classes and iteratively issues prompts to a SAM predictor to obtain structure-specific mask observations with confidence scores. Each observation is fused into the posterior through a stable logit-space evidence accumulation rule, preserving global competition among structures. To enable efficient scanning, a lightweight proposal policy is learned to select the next target structure and prompt location conditioned on the current posterior and its uncertainty, trained by supervised imitation from step-wise oracle actions defined by posterior residuals. Experiments on dense abdominal and fetal cardiac ultrasound planes demonstrate that ScanSeg consistently outperforms both single-shot and prompted baselines, yielding more reliable fine-grained multi-structure segmentation and improving average Dice by up to 6.52 points on Abdomen and 4.94 points on A4C with only a few predictor calls.

title: Uncertainty-guided Multitask Mean Teacher Model for Hybrid ASPECTS Scoring of Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: The Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) is crucial for accurate diagnosis and treatment decision-making in acute ischemic stroke. Recent hybrid scoring methods that combine ASPECTS prediction with auxiliary lesion segmentation have demonstrated great potential by enhancing the model's discriminative power through multitask learning. However, their performance is still limited by the scarcity of labeled data and the insufficient exploitation of shared information across tasks, posing challenges for precise and robust stroke assessment. In this paper, we propose a novel semi-supervised hybrid ASPECTS scoring framework (Semi-HAS) built upon an uncertainty guided multitask mean teacher architecture, which leverages readily available unlabeled data to enhance ASPECTS scoring. Specifically, a dedicated task interaction component is introduced in Semi-HAS to explicitly extract lesion-related complementary information from the auxiliary segmentation task. The proposed component is meanwhile coordinated with a cross-task alignment loss to successfully facilitate collaboration between different tasks for more consistent ASPECTS prediction. Furthermore, we design an adaptive uncertainty estimation for both tasks to generate dual uncertainty maps for mitigating noise introduced by unlabeled data. As a result, this innovative strategy effectively guides cross-model consistency learning for transferring trustworthy knowledge from teacher to student model and improving scoring accuracy for complex anatomical conditions. Extensive experiments on both public and in-house datasets demonstrate that Semi-HAS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods by achieving superior scoring accuracy across ASPECTS regions and providing reliable patient level assessments, highlighting its promise in facilitating clinical ASPECTS evaluation and promoting personalized treatments.

title: FocFormer-UNet: UNet With Focal Modulation and Transformers for Ultrasound Needle Tracking Using Photoacoustic Ground Truth.
abstract: Objective Ultrasound (US)-guided needle tracking is a critical procedure for various clinical diagnoses and treatment planning, highlighting the need for improved visualization methods to enhance accuracy. While deep learning (DL) techniques have been employed to boost needle visibility in US images, they often rely heavily on manual annotations or simulated datasets, which can introduce biases and limit real-world applicability. Photoacoustic (PA) imaging, known for its high contrast capabilities, offers a promising solution by providing superior needle visualization compared to conventional US images. Methods In this work, we present FocFormer-UNet, a DL network that leverages PA images of the needle as ground truth for training, eliminating the need for manual annotations. This approach significantly improves needle localization accuracy in US images, reducing the reliance on time-consuming manual labeling. Results FocFormer-UNet achieves excellent needle localization accuracy, demonstrated by a modified Hausdorff distance of 1.43$\pm$ 1.23 and a targeting error of 1.22$\pm$ 1.14 on human clinical dataset, indicating minimal deviation from actual needle positions. Conclusion Our method offers robust needle tracking across diverse US systems, improving the precision and reliability of US-guided needle insertion procedures. It holds great promise for advancing AI-driven clinical support tools in medical imaging.

title: Segment Anything Model 2: An Application to 2D and 3D Medical Images.
abstract: Segment Anything Model (SAM) has gained significant attention because of its ability to segment a variety of objects in images upon providing a prompt. Recently developed SAM 2 has extended this ability to video segmentation, and by substituting the third spatial dimension in 3D images for the time dimension in videos, it opens an opportunity to apply SAM 2 to 3D medical images. In this paper, we extensively evaluate SAM 2's ability to segment both 2D and 3D medical images using 80 prompt strategies across 21 medical imaging datasets, including 2D modalities (X-ray and ultrasound), 3D modalities (magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, and positron emission tomography), and surgical videos. We find that in the 2D setting, SAM 2 performs similarly to SAM, while in the 3D setting we observe that: (1) selecting the first mask is more effective than choosing the one with the highest confidence, (2) prompting the slice with the largest object appears is the most cost-effective strategy when only one slice is prompted, (3) box prompts result in higher performance than point prompts at a slightly higher annotation cost, (4) bidirectional propagation outperforms front-to-end propagation, (5) interactive annotation is rarely effective, (6) SAM 2, without fine-tuning, achieves 3D IoU from 0.32 with a single point prompt to 0.51 with a ground truth mask on one slice, and exceeds 0.8 on certain datasets when using box or ground-truth prompts, a level that begins to approach clinical usefulness. These findings demonstrate that SAM 2's ability to segment 3D medical images can be improved with our proposed strategies over the default ones, providing practical guidance for using SAM 2 for prompt-based 3D medical image segmentation.

title: PINN-EM: Physics-Guided Disease Progression Model of Geographic Atrophy.
abstract: Objective To construct a personalizable spatio-temporal disease progression model of patients with a late dry form of Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD), known as Geographic Atrophy (GA). Methods From a series of retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans, we infer the coefficients for the parametrized partial differential equation (PDE), such that the parametrized PDE best describes the observed imaging data. Acting as a soft constraint, the recovered PDE helps to extrapolate an implicit neural representation (INR) of the GA segmentation map progression. To enable efficient training, we propose an iterative method - PINN-EM, designed to recover coefficients of non-linear PDEs. At each iteration, the method decouples the problem into PDE coefficients fitting and data fitting steps, resembling Expectation Maximization algorithm. Results We extensively tested the proposed method in large-scale experiments using the open-source PDEBench benchmark to validate its performance. Furthermore, we applied the method to the challenging problem of GA progression modeling, where patients exhibit a high variance in GA growth patterns and speed. The proposed spatio-temporal disease progression model outperformed the baselines, even outperforming posterior knowledge models in Dice score for newly affected growth areas. Conclusion We demonstrated that the proposed spatio-temporal disease progression model fitted with introduced PINN-EM outperforms existing baselines in synthetic and real clinical applications, highlighting the extrapolation capabilities of the INR models. Significance The proposed spatio-temporal disease progression model and PINN-EM fitting procedure can be applied across diverse domains facing the challenge of fitting parametrized PDE to the empirical datasets.

title: LDiT3D: Head and Neck Tumor Segmentation Using a 3D Latent Diffusion Transformer Model.
abstract: Objective Head and neck (H&N) tumors are among the most common cancers worldwide. However, manual annotation of H&N tumors for each patient poses a significant burden on clinicians. Therefore, developing automated and accurate methods for H&N tumor segmentation is of great clinical importance. Methods We introduce LDiT3D, a novel 3D transformer-based diffusion model designed to segment H&N tumors from 3D Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and X-ray computed tomography (CT) scans, primarily focusing on oropharyngeal tumors. LDiT3D utilizes stacked 3D vision transformer blocks to effectively capture spatial context in volumetric data. To address the high computational cost typically associated with 3D transformers, we incorporate a pre-trained autoencoder that projects the input into a lower-dimensional latent space where the diffusion process is performed more efficiently. In addition to the diffusion loss computed in latent space, a task-specific segmentation loss is introduced in pixel space to further enhance segmentation accuracy. Results Methods based on U-Net and transformer architectures were selected as reference methods. Comparative results demonstrated that the proposed LDiT3D achieved highly accurate segmentation performance, with the highest Dice Score and lowest Hausdorff distance on both public and local datasets. Moreover, LDiT3D showed a more balanced performance between Precision and Recall, as indicated by the highest Fowlkes-Mallows Score. Ablation studies further confirmed the effectiveness of the key components in the LDiT3D design. Conclusion LDiT3D delivers more accurate and balanced H&N tumor segmentation compared to reference methods. Significance These findings highlight LDiT3D's potential to improve automated H&N tumor annotation and advance medical image analysis.

title: DPSeg: Differentiated Perception Medical Image Segmentation via Context-Aware Compensation and Stratified Uncertainty Attention.
abstract: In medical image segmentation, accurate recognition of regions hindered by blurry boundaries, low contrast, and complex backgrounds is crucial. These issues lead to significant differences in segmentation difficulty within a single image. However, existing methods typically adopt a uniform modeling strategy across the entire feature map, overlooking the mismatch between segmentation difficulty and attention intensity. Consequently, they fail to adequately focus on key regions, diluting the representations of challenging regions. To address these challenges, we propose DPSeg, a differentiated perception medical image segmentation framework via context-aware compensation and stratified uncertainty attention. Specifically, DPSeg comprises three key components. The Context-Aware Compensation (CAC) module refines encoder features by integrating key region-aware prompts and contextual information, compensating for encoding-induced distortions and enabling differentiated perception, thereby providing higher-quality representations for decoding. Additionally, the Stratified Uncertainty Transformer (SUTrans) module explicitly modulates the attention intensity of different regions based on their segmentation uncertainty, thereby possessing differentiated perception ability while effectively suppressing redundant feature interactions. Moreover, we propose a Foreground-Uncertainty Adaptive Weighted Loss (FUAWL) to enable differentiated supervision across decoding stages, applying stronger guidance to uncertain regions in shallow decoding and emphasizing foreground regions in deep decoding to improve boundary delineation and mitigate foreground-background imbalance. Extensive experiments on four challenging datasets demonstrate that DPSeg achieves competitive segmentation performance.

Consequently, they fail to adequately focus on key regions, diluting the representations of challenging regions. To address these challenges, we propose DPSeg, a differentiated perception medical image segmentation framework via context-aware compensation and stratified uncertainty attention. Specifically, DPSeg comprises three key components. The Context-Aware Compensation (CAC) module refines encoder features by integrating key region-aware prompts and contextual information, compensating for encoding-induced distortions and enabling differentiated perception, thereby providing higher-quality representations for decoding. Additionally, the Stratified Uncertainty Transformer (SUTrans) module explicitly modulates the attention intensity of different regions based on their segmentation uncertainty, thereby possessing differentiated perception ability while effectively suppressing redundant feature interactions. Moreover, we propose a Foreground-Uncertainty Adaptive Weighted Loss (FUAWL) to enable differentiated supervision across decoding stages, applying stronger guidance to uncertain regions in shallow decoding and emphasizing foreground regions in deep decoding to improve boundary delineation and mitigate foreground-background imbalance. Extensive experiments on four challenging datasets demonstrate that DPSeg achieves competitive segmentation performance.

title: ZonoSeg: A Zonal-aware Prostate Segmentation Framework on 3D MRI images.
abstract: Accurate zonal-aware prostate segmentation in clinical 3D MRI is important for diagnosis and treatment planning. However, delineating the central-gland-peripheral-zone interface remains challenging because gradual tissue transitions, irregular internal boundaries, and pathology-induced appearance variations can lead to clinically relevant zonal boundary errors. We propose ZonoSeg, a hierarchical encoder-decoder framework that targets these ambiguous boundaries via uncertainty-aware, boundary-sensitive feature transmission in stage-wise skip connections. The ZonoSeg Block combines edge cues with learnable multi-scale Gaussian smoothing to construct a continuous probabilistic boundary field, and the ZAD head further refines zonal separation through explicit foreground-background interactions. Experiments demonstrate improved boundary localization and robust zonal segmentation on both dual-target and single-target tasks across eight multi-center prostate MRI datasets; on PROMISE MRI BMC, ZonoSeg achieves Dice scores of 83.39% for the central gland and 84.10% for the peripheral zone, with HD95 of 3.84 mm and 3.41 mm, respectively. Code: https://github.com/deepang-ai/ZonoSeg.

title: Decoupling Multi-Contrast Super-Resolution: Self-Supervised Implicit Re-Representation for Unpaired Cross-Modal Synthesis.
abstract: Multi-contrast super-resolution (MCSR) is crucial for enhancing MRI but current deep learning methods are limited. They typically require large, paired low- and high-resolution (LR/HR) training datasets, which are scarce, and are trained for fixed upsampling scales. While recent self-supervised methods remove the paired data requirement, they fail to leverage valuable population-level priors. In this work, we propose a novel, decoupled MCSR framework that resolves both limitations. We reformulate MCSR into two stages: (1) an unpaired cross-modal synthesis (uCMS) module, trained once on unpaired population data to learn a robust anatomical prior; and (2) a lightweight, patient-specific implicit re-representation (IrR) module. This IrR module is optimized in a self-supervised manner to fuse the population prior with the subject's own LR target data. This design uniquely fuses population-level knowledge with patient-specific fidelity without requiring paired target-domain LR/HR training data or paired cross-modal HR reference-target training data. Here, 'unpaired' refers to the population-level training setting; at subject-specific inference, as in standard MCSR, the method uses a matched HR reference image from another contrast together with the subject's LR target image. By building the IrR module on an implicit neural representation, our framework is also inherently scale-agnostic. Our method demonstrates superior quantitative performance on different datasets, with exceptional robustness at extreme scales (16×, 32×), a regime where competing methods fail. Our work presents a data-efficient, flexible, and computationally lightweight paradigm for MCSR, enabling high-fidelity, arbitrary-scale reconstruction without the need for paired population-level supervision.

title: EM-SliceCrafter: Distilling Lightweight 2D CNNs for Efficient 3D EM Neuron Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate 3D neuron segmentation from large-scale electron microscopy (EM) volumes is a cornerstone of connectomics, yet it is hampered by a trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency. While 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) offer high accuracy by predicting 3D affinity maps, their high computational cost and limited input size impede their application to large-scale data. To overcome this, we introduce EM-SliceCrafter, a novel framework that employs a lightweight 2D CNN for both efficient and precise 3D neuron segmentation. Our method generates a 3D affinity map by computing distances between embedding maps of adjacent 2D slices. To enrich the 2D network's contextual understanding, we propose a dual-distillation strategy. First, Cross-Dimension Affinity Distillation (CAD) transfers inter-slice structural knowledge from a 3D teacher network to enhance 3D continuity. Complementarily, Internal-Dimension Affinity Distillation (IAD) leverages a powerful teacher built on the pre-trained Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) encoder, using a learnable adapter, to distill fine-grained intra-slice boundary details. Furthermore, a Feature Grafting Interaction (FGI) module deepens knowledge transfer by integrating embeddings across the student and both teacher networks. Extensive experiments on diverse EM datasets, featuring various imaging modalities and resolutions, show that EM-SliceCrafter improves segmentation accuracy over state-of-the-art methods while achieving a 33× speedup in GPU forward inference. The code is available at https://github.com/liuxy1103/EM-SliceCrafter.

title: Multiparameter Uncertainty Mapping in Quantitative Molecular MRI using a Physics-Structured Variational Autoencoder (PS-VAE).
abstract: Quantitative imaging methods, such as magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF), aim to extract interpretable pathology biomarkers by estimating biophysical tissue parameters from signal evolutions. However, the pattern-matching algorithms or neural networks used in such inverse problems often lack principled uncertainty quantification, which limits the trustworthiness and transparency, required for clinical acceptance. Here, we describe a physics-structured variational autoencoder (PS-VAE) designed for rapid extraction of voxelwise multi-parameter posterior distributions. Our approach integrates a differentiable spin physics simulator with self-supervised learning, and provides a full covariance that captures the inter-parameter correlations in the latent biophysical space. The method was validated in a multi-proton pool chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) and semisolid magnetization transfer (MT) molecular MRF study, across in-vitro phantoms, tumor-bearing mice, healthy human volunteers, and subjects with glioblastoma and Alzheimer's Disease. The resulting multi-parametric posteriors are in good agreement with those calculated using a brute-force Bayesian analysis, while providing an orders-of-magnitude acceleration in whole brain quantification. In addition, we demonstrate how monitoring the multi-parameter posterior dynamics across progressively acquired signals provides practical insights for protocol optimization and may facilitate real-time adaptive acquisition. The code and sample data are available at https://github.com/momentum-laboratory/ps-vae.

title: EyeGraph: A Multi-granularity Medical Vision-Language Foundation Model with Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Ophthalmic Interpretation.
abstract: The exponential growth of large vision-language models (VLMs) has created significant opportunities for advancing multimodal artificial intelligence in specialized domains such as ophthalmology. However, progress in ophthalmic VLMs remains limited, primarily due to the lack of large-scale, high-quality image-text pairs. Moreover, existing VLMs frequently generate hallucinations, leading to uncertainty and unreliability that are unacceptable in clinical practice. To address the data scarcity issue, we introduce IT-Retinal, a dedicated ophthalmic Vision Question Answering (VQA) dataset that providesmultigranularity tasks and high-quality long-form textual content in image-text pairs. To mitigate hallucinations, we propose EyeGraph, a framework for ophthalmic VLMs that consists of two training stages, targeted pre-training and fine-tuning, and one inference stage that integrates Graph of Thought (GoT) and Think on Graph (ToG) reasoning, referred to as G2T. This design enables EyeGraph to incorporate structured external knowledge, constrain the output space, and produce more clinically consistent results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EyeGraph achieves state-of-the-art performance across seven clinically relevant benchmarks, spanning disease diagnosis, structural detection and localization, and report generation. Notably, the proposed G2T reasoning module consistently improves the factual consistency and reliability of ophthalmic report generation. All source code, along with an interactive demo, is publicly available at: https://github.com/ZardCAI/EyeGraph.
