title: Latent Interpolation Learning Using Diffusion Models for Cardiac Volume Reconstruction.
abstract: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) imaging is a critical tool for diagnosing and managing cardiovascular disease, yet its utility is often limited by the sparse acquisition of 2D short-axis slices, resulting in incomplete volumetric information. Accurate 3D reconstruction from these sparse slices is essential for comprehensive cardiac assessment, but existing methods face challenges, including reliance on predefined interpolation schemes (e.g., linear or spherical), computational inefficiency, and dependence on additional semantic inputs such as segmentation labels or motion data. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Cardiac Latent Interpolation Diffusion (CaLID) framework that introduces three key innovations. First, we present a data-driven interpolation scheme based on diffusion models, which can capture complex, non-linear relationships between sparse slices and improves reconstruction accuracy. Second, we design a computationally efficient method that operates in the latent space and speeds up generative 3D whole-heart upsampling time by a factor of 24, reducing computational overhead compared to previous methods. Third, with only sparse 2D CMR images as input, our method achieves SOTA performance against baseline methods, eliminating the need for auxiliary input such as morphological guidance, thus simplifying workflows. We further extend our method to 2D+T data, enabling the effective modeling of spatiotemporal dynamics and ensuring temporal coherence. Extensive volumetric evaluations and downstream segmentation tasks demonstrate that CaLID achieves superior reconstruction quality and efficiency. By addressing the fundamental limitations of existing approaches, our framework advances the state of the art for spatio and spatiotemporal whole-heart reconstruction, offering a robust and clinically practical solution for cardiovascular imaging. The code is available at https://github.com/niklasbubeck/calid.

title: PARDA: A Perceive-Act-Reflect-Distill Agent for Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation.
abstract: Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (SFUDA) has emerged as a critical paradigm for addressing severe domain shifts in medical image segmentation under strict data privacy constraints, where source data are inaccessible. However, existing SFUDA methods primarily rely on static, open-loop adaptation pipelines, lacking the ability to actively perceive target domain characteristics and use reflection to correct accumulated errors. Meanwhile, Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit strong generalization across modalities and anatomies, yet their high computational inference overhead and deployment constraints prevent direct adoption on clinical edge devices. In this work, we propose PARDA, a VLM-coupled closed-loop SFUDA framework for medical image segmentation. PARDA reformulates SFUDA as a closed-loop decision-making process, in which the method actively perceives target domain characteristics, acts by coordinating semantic and geometric VFMs to generate pseudo-labels, reflects on the reliability of its anatomical and structural representations to guide refinement, and finally distills the acquired adaptation knowledge into a lightweight student model. This design enables PARDA to mitigate error accumulation while preserving data privacy and inference efficiency. We conduct a comprehensive SFUDA evaluation covering 13 cross-modality domain adaptation directions and 24 anatomical targets across diverse organs and imaging modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that PARDA achieves robust and universal domain adaptation while distilling the adaptation results into a lightweight student model for resource-constrained inference.

title: Noise2Match: Self-Supervised Low-Dose CT Denoising via Adaptive Inter-Slice Matching.
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning, supervised convolutional neural network methods have greatly improved the performance of low-dose computed tomography (CT) denoising. However, they require paired noisy-clean training data, which is difficult to obtain in practice. Some classic self-supervised denoising methods rely on the assumption of pixel-wise independent noise, making them ineffective for correlated noise in low-dose CT (LDCT) images. Considering the high similarity and weaker noise correlation between adjacent CT slices, several recently proposed self-supervised methods use adjacent LDCT slices for training. Nevertheless, these approaches fail to effectively account for the non-rigid mis-alignment between slices caused by anatomical variation, hindering them from satisfying the equal-mean condition required by the classic Noise2Noise framework. In this paper, we propose Noise2Match, a self-supervised LDCT denoising method based on adaptive inter-slice matching. Noise2Match introduces an inter-slice matching network to model the label transition process between adjacent slices, and then applies correction to the denoiser's outputs to better satisfy the equal-mean condition. We theoretically prove that, under idealized conditions, training Noise2Match using adjacent LDCT slices is equivalent to supervised training with paired noisy-clean images. We further find that Noise2Match can also effectively perform low-dose cone-beam CT (CBCT) denoising, which could be attributed to its correction operation that reduces inter-slice noise correlation. To the best of our knowledge, Noise2Match is the first effective image-domain self-supervised method for low-dose CBCT. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Noise2Match outperforms existing image-domain self-supervised methods, offering broader applicability and higher practical value.

title: Stochastic Siamese MAE Pretraining for Longitudinal Medical Images.
abstract: Temporally aware image representations are crucial for capturing disease progression in 3D volumes of longitudinal medical datasets. However, recent state-of-the-art self-supervised learning approaches like Masked Autoencoding (MAE), despite their strong representation learning capabilities, lack temporal awareness. In this paper, we propose STAMP (Stochastic Temporal Autoencoder with Masked Pretraining), a Siamese MAE framework that encodes temporal information through a stochastic process by conditioning on the time difference between the 2 input volumes. Unlike deterministic Siamese approaches, which compare scans from different time points but fail to account for the inherent uncertainty in disease evolution, STAMP learns temporal dynamics stochastically by reframing the MAE reconstruction loss as a conditional variational inference objective. We evaluated STAMP on two OCT and one MRI datasets with multiple visits per patient. STAMP pretrained ViT models outperformed both existing temporal MAE methods and foundation models on different late stage Age-Related Macular Degeneration and Alzheimer's Disease progression prediction which require models to learn the underlying non-deterministic temporal dynamics of the diseases.

title: Tomographic Sparse View Selection Using the View Covariance Loss.
abstract: Standard computed tomography (CT) reconstruction algorithms such as filtered back projection (FBP) and Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) require many views for producing high-quality reconstructions, which can slow image acquisition and increase cost in non-destructive evaluation (NDE) applications. Over the past 20 years, a variety of methods have been developed for computing high-quality CT reconstructions from sparse views. However, the problem of how to select the best views for CT reconstruction remains open. In this paper, we present a novel view covariance loss (VCL) function that measures the joint information of a set of views by approximating the normalized mean squared error (NMSE) of the reconstruction. We present fast algorithms for computing the VCL along with an algorithm for selecting a subset of views that approximately minimizes its value. Our experiments on simulated and measured data indicate that for a fixed number of views our proposed view covariance loss selection (VCLS) algorithm results in reconstructions with lower NRMSE, fewer artifacts, and greater accuracy than current alternative approaches.

title: Negation-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models.
abstract: In this paper, we study a practical but less-touched problem in Vision-Language Models (VLMs), i.e., negation understanding. Specifically, many real-world applications require models to explicitly identify what is false or non-existent, e.g., radiologists may search for images that exclude specific conditions. Despite the impressive transferability of VLMs through large-scale training, they suffer from a critical limitation that fails to handle negation. To address this challenge, existing methods attribute its root cause to the scarcity of negation training data and propose to fine-tune VLMs on massive data containing explicit negation. Undoubtedly, such data-centric solutions demand substantial data and computational resources, limiting their sustainable widespread adoption. To tackle negation in a low-carbon manner, we empirically observe that the key obstacle lies in the dual-concept shifts between the affirmation and negation distributions. Therefore, we propose a Negation-Aware Test-Time Adaptation (NEAT) method to efficiently adjust distribution-related parameters during inference. In brief, NEAT can reduce distribution shift in consistent semantics while eliminating false distributional consistency in unrelated semantics. Extensive experiments on the various negation understanding tasks verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Remarkably, with less than 0.01% of trainable parameters, NEAT achieves comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art post-training approaches.

Despite the impressive transferability of VLMs through large-scale training, they suffer from a critical limitation that fails to handle negation. To address this challenge, existing methods attribute its root cause to the scarcity of negation training data and propose to fine-tune VLMs on massive data containing explicit negation. Undoubtedly, such data-centric solutions demand substantial data and computational resources, limiting their sustainable widespread adoption. To tackle negation in a low-carbon manner, we empirically observe that the key obstacle lies in the dual-concept shifts between the affirmation and negation distributions. Therefore, we propose a Negation-Aware Test-Time Adaptation (NEAT) method to efficiently adjust distribution-related parameters during inference. In brief, NEAT can reduce distribution shift in consistent semantics while eliminating false distributional consistency in unrelated semantics. Extensive experiments on the various negation understanding tasks verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Remarkably, with less than 0.01% of trainable parameters, NEAT achieves comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art post-training approaches.

title: RAC-Net: Interpretable Medical Small Target Segmentation Network With X-Ray Radiation Attenuation Characterization.
abstract: Medical image target segmentation is critical for clinical diagnosis and treatment, yet mainstream methods perform poorly on small medical targets due to inefficient sparse feature extraction and severe background interference. To tackle this issue, we propose Radiation Attenuation Characteristics Network (RAC-Net) inspired by the X-ray attenuation physical prior in CT imaging, aiming to boost small target segmentation accuracy for early lesion detection and localization. Specifically, RAC-Net integrates two tailored innovative modules: the Radiation Attenuation Salient Feature Extraction (RASFE) module leverages X-ray attenuation principles to extract small target Gaussian saliency features and suppress background noise, enhancing sparse feature representation; the Partial Volume Artifact Edge Enhancement (PVA) module embedded with CT Hounsfield Unit value prior fuses learnable neighborhood weights and physical prior weights, alleviating feature distortion and edge blurring caused by partial volume artifacts, while improving model robustness via clinical medical priors. Extensive experiments validate that RAC-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance in medical small target segmentation, with 18% DICE and 19% IOU improvements over advanced existing methods, providing solid support for early disease diagnosis and intervention.

title: Towards Medical Image Dataset Distillation: A Progressive Trajectory Matching and Dynamic Diversity Enhancing Method.
abstract: Sharing medical image sets is essential yet challenging due to limited resource and strict regulatory, which significantly hinder the development of medical foundation models and the transfer of medical domain knowledge. In this paper, we utilize medical image dataset distillation techniques to enable effective model construction and knowledge transfer without requiring downstream users to directly access the original data. Trajectory matching has become the mainstream distillation technique, yet our empirical findings on medical image datasets reveal two critical phenomena: instability of distillation optimization and redundancy of synthetic images. To investigate these phenomena, we conduct a theoretical analysis from the perspectives of bi-level optimization and neural tangent kernel, and formally define them as two core challenges: trajectory matching drift and intra-class diversity decay, which underscore the need for more stable and diversity-preserving trajectory matching methods. Guided by the analysis results, we propose a novel progressive and diverse dataset distillation (PD$^{3}$) method, which incorporates (1) a progressive trajectory matching paradigm that progressively unrolls the student training trajectory to extend the matching horizon, while adaptively selecting optimal expert matching trajectory to ensure stable and convergent distillation optimization; and (2) a dynamic diversity enhancing module that alleviates the redundancy of synthetic images by enhancing intra-class distribution and breaking redundancy accumulation. To facilitate fair evaluation, we establish a comprehensive medical image dataset distillation benchmark covering diverse medical image modalities. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method achieves an average absolute improvement of 10.20% and a relative gain of 20.09% over prior state-of-the-art methods, highlighting its effectiveness and practical potential.

title: Intelligent Diagnosis of Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions Based on Endobronchial Ultrasound Images Using Multi-modal Features.
abstract: Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. For peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) that cannot be definitively diagnosed by computed tomography (CT) or positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) imaging, endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial lung biopsy (EBUS-TBLB) for pathological examinations still carries a significant possibility of indefinite diagnosis. Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) serves as not only a valuable and widely used guidance technique but also a superior diagnostic technique for PPLs compared with CT or PET-CT, by enabling direct visualization of the structures within the lesion and the echo distributions outside the lesion. Aimed at classifying PPLs as benign or malignant, this study enrolled 313 patients for the final analysis. Multi-modal features including clinical, radiomic, and deep features were integrated and fed into an artificial neural network for feature selection, fusion, and prediction based on the long-axis diameter of PPLs measured on CT images with a threshold of 3 cm. To reduce manual effort and maximize the diagnostic performance of multi-modal features, we employed the particle swarm optimization algorithm to automatically optimize the combination of selected features and model structure. Our method achieves an average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.981 (95% CI: 0.953-1.000), accuracy of 0.964, sensitivity of 0.963, specificity of 0.969, and F1-score of 0.976 on the independent test dataset after four-fold cross-validation. The outstanding diagnostic performance for PPLs based on EBUS images, with all the evaluation metrics exceeding 0.95, can provide a solid foundation for clinical decision-making, biopsy site selection, and follow-up observations.

title: Compound Lens Design and Beamforming for Wide-Field Volumetric Imaging Using a Row-Column Array.
abstract: Row-column addressed (RCA) ultrasound arrays enable volumetric imaging with a significantly reduced channel count compared to fully addressed 2-D arrays; however, their field of view (FOV) is typically limited to the transducer footprint. Diverging acoustic lenses can extend the FOV, but accurate beamforming remains challenging when the lens's finite thickness and multilayer structure are not properly modeled. This work presents a compound acoustic lens design that simultaneously achieves a large FOV, reduced edge-wave artifacts, and acceptable sensitivity loss, together with a beamforming approach that accurately accounts for wave propagation through multilayer lens structures. The proposed approach combines ray tracing with a Normal Path (RT-NP) approximation and determines the optimal propagation path using a two-dimensional Newton-Raphson optimization, enabling accurate time-of-flight (TOF) estimation while significantly reducing computational complexity compared to conventional two-interface ray-tracing methods. The method is validated experimentally using a 128+128 Vermon RCA transducer operating at 6 MHz and equipped with a BiQuadratic compound lens composed of TPX and RTV-PTFE materials. Pressure-field measurements validate the predicted wavefront expansion, while simulations indicate an FOV expansion to approximately 54.5°, enabling imaging well beyond the transducer aperture while preserving high spatial resolution and image quality. Hydrophone and RF-data measurements demonstrate sub-wavelength TOF accuracy of the proposed beamformer. The proposed system achieves a penetration depth of 75 mm compared with 90 mm without the lens, with only minor degradation in spatial resolution. These results demonstrate that compound-lens RCA systems, combined with accurate and efficient beamforming, enable wide-field volumetric imaging of organ-scale structures while preserving the practical advantages of RCA arrays, with a theoretical volume rate of approximately 104 Hz, indicating the potential for real-time 3-D visualization.

title: Automated Volumetric ROI Selection for Ultrasound Attenuation-Based Assessment of Liver Steatosis.
abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) attenuation imaging is a promising low-cost approach for hepatic steatosis assessment, but current methods remain sensitive to operator-defined region-of-interest (ROI) selection and may not fully exploit volumetric acquisitions. We present an automated multi-plane attenuation-coefficient estimation (ACE) method for matrix-array ultrasound that defines and refines the attenuation ROI through learning-based liver masking, vessel exclusion, axial range detection, model-based Aline rejection, and robust plane aggregation. The method was tuned and tested in phantoms and subsequently evaluated against same-visit MRI proton-density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) in 35 subjects with 237 volumetric acquisitions. Subject-level ACE was defined as the median across repeated acquisitions, and repeatability was quantified using the within-subject coefficient of variation (CV). Subject-level ACE was associated with MRI-PDFF, yielding Pearson r = 0.8835 (95% CI, 0.8182-0.9349), Spearman ρ = 0.9135 (95% CI, 0.7926-0.9579), and R 2 = 0.7806. The mean within-subject CV was 3.24% (95% CI, 2.82-3.67%). AUCs were 0.958 (95% CI, 0.871-1.000) for distinguishing S1+ from S0 at MRI-PDFF ≥ 6% and 0.954 (95% CI, 0.878-1.000) for distinguishing S2+ from S0/S1 at MRI-PDFF ≥ 17%. These findings support the feasibility of an automated post-acquisition volumetric attenuation-imaging pipeline that reduces dependence on manual ROI selection for quantitative liver fat assessment.

title: Boiling Histotripsy with 1.1/3.3 MHz Dual-Frequency Inducing Long-Duration Anti-Tumor Immunity in Mice Breast Cancer.
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) has a poor prognosis and high risk of recurrence and metastasis. Histotripsy is an ultrasound-guided, non-invasive, non-thermal ablation method that mechanically lyses target tissues. A boiling histotripsy (DF-MS BH) technique combining 1.1/3.3 MHz superposition with a multi-stage ultrasound pulse scheme was proposed, aiming to enhance anti-tumor immune response by optimizing pulse dose and number of treatments. A custom-designed 1.1-/3.3-MHz two-element confocal-annular array and multi-stage ultrasound pulses were used for treatment. For 6-mm-diameter tumors, the ablated volume accounted for 60-70 % of the total tumor volume. The anti-tumor immune results showed increasing pulse dose from 85 to 115 elevated DAMPs release and reduced tumor growth rate. After the first high-dose pulse treatment, the infiltration level of CD8 + T cells gradually increased and then decreased on the 7th day, which contributed to a 9-day period of tumor growth arrest. Following the second treatment, the release of danger signals was further augmented. Meanwhile, the high-level infiltration of CD8 + T cells persisted for 35 days, extending the tumor growth arrest period to 25 days and prolonging the median survival period of mice to 50 days. In addition, this treatment strategy effectively reduced the number of lung metastases, confirming its ability to enhance systemic anti-tumor immune response. Furthermore, DF-MS BH ameliorated the immunosuppressive microenvironment of TNBC through first and second enhanced treatments. Ultimately, the combination therapy of DF-MS BH and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) further suppressed tumor recurrence and metastasis.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Full-Length BP180 and Native BP180-α6β4 Integrin Complex ELISAs in Serologically Inconclusive Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid.
abstract: Mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP) is a chronic autoimmune subepithelial blistering disorder of mucosal surfaces that can cause irreversible scarring, blindness, or dysphagia. Early diagnosis is challenging because histopathology is nonspecific and conventional BP180 NC16A ELISAs have limited sensitivity. We evaluated ELISAs using full-length recombinant BP180 and a native BP180-α6β4 integrin complex in six patients with suspected oral or ocular MMP. The conventional NC16A ELISA was negative in four of six patients, and biopsy alone was often insufficient. Both assays provided useful serological support in a subset of cases when interpreted alongside direct immunofluorescence (DIF) and clinical phenotype, whereas in others DIF remained the primary basis for diagnosis. These assays can therefore complement, but not replace, clinicopathological assessment in suspected MMP.

title: Green Ultrasound-Assisted Extraction of Bioactive Phenolics From Quince (Cydonia oblonga) Leaves: Multi-Response Optimization, LC-MS/MS Profiling, and Comparison With Conventional Methods.
abstract: Quince (Cydonia oblonga Mill.) leaves are an abundant yet underutilized agricultural by-product that is rich in phenolic compounds and therefore represents a promising feedstock for value-added bioactive extracts. This study optimized the green ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) of bioactive compounds from quince leaves using a sequential statistical approach based on Plackett-Burman screening and Taguchi-based criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC)-weighted grey relational analysis (GRA). Under the optimum conditions (solid-to-liquid ratio 3:50 g/mL, 50% (v/v) ethanol, and 75°C), the extract exhibited a total phenolic content (TPC) of 9210.44 ± 138.25 mg GAE L - 1 , a total flavonoid content (TFC) of 6180.67 ± 94.25 mg CE L - 1 and a DPPH free radical-scavenging capacity of 76.53 ± 3.65 mmol TE L - 1 . Triplicate confirmation experiments validated the model, with an overall prediction accuracy of 97.69%. Ethanol concentration exerted the greatest influence on the grey relational grade (36.28%). Under identical operating conditions, the optimized UAE provided the most balanced extraction performance. It yielded the highest TPC, antioxidant activity, anti-inflammatory activity, and α-amylase inhibition relative to maceration, magnetic stirring, hand-shaking, and reflux, while LC-MS/MS identified quinic and chlorogenic acids as the principal constituents. These results indicate that the UAE optimized through a Taguchi-based CRITIC-weighted GRA is an effective and sustainable strategy for producing bioactive-rich extracts from quince-leaf waste. PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS: This study provides a practical, statistically grounded route for converting quince (Cydonia oblonga Mill.) leaf waste, an abundant agro-industrial by-product, into phenolic-rich extracts using a green, food-grade ultrasound-assisted process. The sequential screening and multi-response optimization framework can be adopted by food, nutraceutical, and functional-ingredient manufacturers to maximize antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and enzyme-inhibitory activities while minimizing solvent and energy use, supporting cost-effective and sustainable valorization of leaf biomass.

title: Bioactive Peptides in Functional Foods: From Production and Validation to Commercialization, Regulatory Hurdles, and Future Prospects.
abstract: Bioactive peptides (BAPs) exhibit a wide range of health-promoting properties, positioning them as key ingredients for the functional food market. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of the BAP landscape, from discovery and production to commercialization and regulation. Conventional and emerging production technologies are critically analyzed, highlighting advancements in enzymatic hydrolysis, microbial fermentation, and physical processing methods like high-pressure and ultrasound-assisted extraction. The multi-tiered validation pipeline, spanning in silico prediction, in vitro screening, and in vivo models, is examined, revealing a significant disconnect between preliminary bioactivity data and demonstrable clinical efficacy, which is a primary cause for regulatory failure. Commercialization is hampered by technical challenges, including poor bioavailability, gastrointestinal instability, and undesirable sensory attributes, which are being addressed by innovative formulation strategies such as nano-encapsulation. A comparative analysis of global regulatory frameworks, particularly the divergent approaches of the US FDA and EU EFSA, underscores the hurdles in substantiating health claims, with a universal demand for rigorous human clinical trials. Finally, the future prospects are explored, identifying critical research gaps and highlighting the transformative potential of AI-driven peptide design and personalized nutrition through nutrigenomics to unlock the full potential of BAPs. The review further links peptide structure to nine major biological activities, critically compares advanced delivery systems and manufacturing scale-up, and extends the regulatory analysis to major Asia-Pacific markets.

title: MR Imaging and Radiomics Features for Predicting Variant Histology of Bladder Cancer: A Single Centre Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: Introduction Compare MRI features of bladder variant histology (VH) and pure urothelial carcinoma (UC) and determine if MRI radiomics features can predict VH. Methods In this retrospective study, cystectomy pathology database search yielded 37 patients with tumours with more than 50% VH and preoperative MRI's. Cystectomy database search yielded 38 consecutive patients with pure UC and preoperative MRI's. Three radiologists characterized MRI T2, diffusion-weighted, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps and postcontrast features of bladder tumours. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet's agreement and intra-class coefficients. Another radiologist segmented bladder tumours and adjacent perivesical fat on T2-weighted and ADC images using radiomics software. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) was used to determine radiomics features that distinguished VH from UC. Fifty datasets were prepared using multiple imputation approach, and variables were normalized for LASSO variable selection. Results Patients with VH (mean age = 68, 54 (72%) men) included squamous cell (n = 17), sarcomatoid (n = 6), plasmacytoid (n = 6), adenocarcinoma (n = 4) and small cell (n = 4) variants. Inter-reader agreement was similar for VH and UC (p > 0.44). All readers characterized all squamous cell carcinoma as T2 intermediate. For two of three readers, 92%-100% of hypoenhancing tumours were VH at pathology whereas 74%-78% of hyperenhancing masses were UC (p = 0.001). Combination of 11 selected radiomics features had AUC of 0.98 for training and 0.95 for validation data for prediction of VH. Conclusion Squamous cell carcinoma was T2 intermediate, and VH was more likely to hypoenhance compared to UC. Our radiomic model had excellent performance for predicting VH.

title: Impact of Breast Density and Other Factors on Mammography Guided Vacuum Assisted Breast Biopsy Microcalcification Retrieval Rates.
abstract: Introduction Mammography guided vacuum-assisted biopsy (MG-VAB) is the preferred method for histological diagnosis of screening mammography detected microcalcifications, yet the influence of breast density as well as other patient and procedure-specific factors on retrieval remains underexplored. The purpose of this study is to assess the impact of patient and procedure-specific factors on MG-VAB microcalcification retrieval rates. Methods A retrospective cohort study of 803 consecutive MG-VAB procedures for breast calcifications performed between August 2017 and May 2023 in the BreastScreen ACT population was conducted. Patient data collected included age, breast density, compressed breast thickness, lesion quadrant, calcification size, nipple-to-lesion distance, biopsy approach, specimen radiography visibility as well as presence on pathology. Bayesian logistic regression with weakly informative priors was applied to estimate microcalcification retrieval rates (MRR) and 90% credible intervals. Results The overall median MRR was 98.27% (790/803). Retrieval remained high across age groups (96.4%-99.6%), breast density (95.1%-98.7%), lesion quadrants (96.8%-99.1%), biopsy approach (97.9%-98.6%). Continuous factors such as compressed breast thickness, calcification size and nipple-to-lesion distance demonstrated stable retrieval across ranges. Conclusion MG-VAB achieves consistently high microcalcification retrieval rates across a range of patient and procedural factors, including breast density. These findings reinforce its role as the first line diagnostic method for screening detected microcalcifications.

title: From Recall to Reassurance: Common Benign Mimics in Breast Screening Assessment-A Pictorial Review.
abstract: Benign breast lesions, anatomical variants, and imaging artefacts can closely mimic malignancy on screening mammography and are a frequent diagnostic challenge in the assessment setting. This pictorial review showcases a spectrum of benign lesions encountered in a high-volume breast screening assessment setting that initially raised suspicion for malignancy but were subsequently confirmed as benign through a combination of digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT), targeted ultrasound, and clinicopathological correlation. Examples include cutaneous lesions, sebaceous cysts, intramammary lymph nodes, hamartomas, fat necrosis, vascular lesions, simple cysts and summation artefact. Through illustrative cases, we highlight key imaging features that support accurate lesion characterization and demonstrate the complementary roles of mammography, DBT, and ultrasound in distinguishing benign entities from breast cancer. Familiarity with these imaging appearances can improve diagnostic confidence, reduce false-positive recalls, and minimize unnecessary biopsies within breast screening programs.

title: Can Simple MRI Characteristics Predict Molecular Subgroups in Paediatric Medulloblastoma?
abstract: Introduction Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant paediatric central nervous system (CNS) tumour and is classified using molecular subgroups: WNT, SHH and non-WNT/non-SHH. Subgroup identification guides prognosis and treatment, but requires molecular testing, which is not universally available. MRI is routine in assessment of CNS tumours, and the MRI characteristics may serve as surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subgrouping. This study aims to use simple MRI surrogate markers identified by Perreault et al., against local medulloblastoma cases and their final molecular outcome. Method Retrospective cohort study of paediatric medulloblastomas at a single tertiary children's hospital between January 2015 and October 2025. MRI studies were reviewed by a paediatric neuroradiologist and a radiology registrar in consensus. Tumours were classified by location (cerebellar hemisphere, cerebellopontine angle/cerebellar peduncle (CP/CPA), or midline/fourth ventricle) and enhancement pattern (minimal/none = < 10%, heterogeneous = 10%-90%, solid = > 90%). Associations between MRI features and molecular subgroup were assessed. Results Twenty-two cases were analysed: SHH 22.7% (5/22), WNT 13.6% (3/22) and non-WNT/non-SHH 63.7% (14/22). Most tumours were midline (90.9%), with two hemispheric lesions and no CP/CPA. Enhancement patterns were heterogeneous (54.5%), solid (36.4%) and minimal/none (9.1%). Hemispheric location was associated with SHH tumours (p = 0.043), and all WNT tumours demonstrated solid enhancement (p = 0.036). No other statistically significant associations were identified. Conclusion MRI characteristics offer promising surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subtype. The only strong predictor we found corresponding with Perreault et al. is that hemispheric lesions are correlated with SHH-activated medulloblastoma. This supports further investigation of MRI markers as non-invasive and preoperative medulloblastoma subgroup prediction.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Scoring System and Exploratory Multiomics in Ankylosing Spondylitis: Hip Severity and Age-at-Severe-Hip-Involvement Stratification.
abstract: Introduction Accurate diagnosis and assessment of hip involvement are important for the clinical management of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). This study aimed to develop and internally validate an artificial intelligence-based Ensemble Scoring System (ESS) for AS diagnosis and hip-disease severity assessment and to explore its association with heterogeneous immune-cell infiltration and age at first documented severe hip involvement. Methods A total of 5721 patients with pelvic radiographs and linked clinical records were retrospectively included. Participants were divided into training and held-out validation cohorts at a 7:3 ratio strictly at the patient level, with no patient or image overlap. Deep-learning features extracted by a convolutional neural network were integrated with clinical variables using XGBoost to construct task-specific ensemble deep-learning (EDL) models. Exploratory proteomic, transcriptomic, single-cell RNA-sequencing, immunohistochemical, and peripheral-blood analyses were performed to investigate AS-related immune infiltration. An exploratory immune ensemble (IE) score was constructed using the monocyte proportion and EDL score. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to examine the association between the IE score and age at severe hip involvement. Results The EDL model achieved AUCs of 0.978 for distinguishing AS from non-AS, 0.990 for identifying hip arthropathy among patients with AS, and 0.996 for identifying BASRI-Hip grade ≥ 3 among patients with hip arthropathy. Monocyte percentage was an influential feature across the three EDL classification tasks. Exploratory multiomics and immunohistochemical analyses showed higher LYN expression in AS than in the corresponding non-AS fracture-control groups and suggested that LYN expression was concentrated predominantly in monocytes. A high IE score was associated with earlier severe hip involvement, with estimated median ages at first documented severe hip involvement of 36 and 50 years in the high- and low-IE-score groups, respectively. This finding represents exploratory risk stratification and does not establish independent prediction of biological disease progression. Conclusions The ESS showed strong internal validation performance for AS diagnosis and hip-disease severity classification. Exploratory analyses linked LYN dysregulation in monocytes with heterogeneous immune infiltration, while the IE score was associated with earlier severe hip involvement. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before clinical application.

title: Nodule Dye-Localization Using Interventional Fluoroscopy for Image-Guided Sublobar Lung Resection.
abstract: Background Precise localization is critical for sublobar resection of small pulmonary nodules. We evaluated the safety, technical efficiency, and clinical outcomes of preoperative percutaneous dye-localization using a cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-enabled flat-panel detector interventional fluoroscopy system in a hybrid operating room (HOR). Methods We retrospectively reviewed 74 consecutive patients (137 lesions) who underwent image-guided localization followed by video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) sublobar resection (wedge resection or segmentectomy) between 2022 and 2023 at Chia-Yi Christian Hospital. Procedural workflow, localization success, surgical margins, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. Results Technical localization success was achieved in 100% of lesions (mean nodule diameter: 8.59 ± 4.85 mm). The procedure required a mean of 1.31 ± 0.67 puncture attempts per lesion at a mean depth of 5.22 ± 1.86 cm. Procedure-related pneumothorax occurred in 29.7% (22/74) of patients, with 14.9% (11/74) requiring pigtail catheter drainage; pneumothorax occurrence was significantly associated with multiple puncture attempts (p < 0.001) and lower-lobe lesions (p = 0.001). Lower-lobe location was significantly associated with requiring more puncture attempts (p = 0.028). For malignant lesions, the mean pathological resection margin was 17.16 ± 8.73 mm, with 92.31% achieving a margin-to-tumor ratio (MTR) ≥ 1. The mean postoperative hospital stay was 3.04 ± 1.16 days. Conclusions Single-stage image-guided dye-localization and VATS sublobar lung resection in an HOR using a biplane CBCT-enabled platform is safe, feasible, and effective. This streamlined workflow ensures high technical success and adequate surgical margins with manageable complications. Further studies are warranted to evaluate long-term oncological outcomes.
